exp_enemy.chaos_hound.lore: Just like our wolves, but they somehow stand on the ceiling.
exp_enemy.chaos_hound.name: Chaos Hound
exp_enemy.construct.lore: A golem built to guard the university halls. It has an extremely tough outer shell and has been given a set of magical cannons to fend off attackers, almost like a mobile version of the colony's own Arcane Sentinels.
exp_enemy.construct.name: Arcane Construct
exp_enemy.crusader.lore: A devoted warrior dedicated to the cause of the kingdom. Great care should be taken when fighting these heavily armed fanatics.
exp_enemy.crusader.name: Crusader
exp_enemy.crystal_bat.lore: An impossible creature made of solid crystal. Somehow it flies with ease throughout the caverns.
exp_enemy.crystal_bat.name: Crystal Bat
exp_enemy.crystal_beast.lore: A cat-like beast that grows horns made of illuminated crystal.
exp_enemy.crystal_beast.name: Crystal Beast
exp_enemy.crystal_golem.lore: The remains of an ancient crystalline mining construct. It can still throw a mean punch.
exp_enemy.crystal_golem.name: Crystal Golem
exp_enemy.crystal_wurm.lore: A large wurm that inhabits the deepest parts of the caverns. It tunnels through the crystal walls with ease.
exp_enemy.crystal_wurm.name: Crystal Wurm
exp_enemy.echo_beast.lore: Wolf-like oddities in the Void known for their echoing howls. Their death wails are piercing, sapping the colonists of their strength.
exp_enemy.echo_beast.name: Echo Beast
exp_enemy.fracture_imp.lore: Imps that seem to rapidly fall in and out of existence.
exp_enemy.fracture_imp.name: Fracture Imp

exp_enemy.fungal_horror.name: Fungal Horror
exp_enemy.glitch_beast.lore: Chaotic beasts that appear to be many different animals at once.
exp_enemy.glitch_beast.name: Glitch Beast
exp_enemy.high_priest.lore: A high-ranking member of the royal clergy. Their divine magic is the only kind permissible in the kingdom, though they are extremely limited in their use. The Crusaders see them as a necessary evil, barely tolerating their presence.
exp_enemy.high_priest.name: High Priest
exp_enemy.hollow_sentinel.lore: Giant eyeballs that float through the Void. They appear wrong, with large black lenses unseen in any other realm. They aren't incredibly dangerous on their own, but be wary of the guardians they call upon.
exp_enemy.hollow_sentinel.name: Hollow Sentinel
exp_enemy.kingdom_guard.lore: A common soldier of the kingdom, armed with a simple spear. These soldiers seem undertrained and poorly equipped, as if the kingdom had no foresight that battles would be fought on this side of their borders.
exp_enemy.kingdom_guard.name: Kingdom Guard
exp_enemy.knight.lore: A seasoned warrior of the kingdom, clad in heavy armor. Their heavy swords easily cleave through the armor of our explorers.
exp_enemy.knight.name: Knight
exp_enemy.lab_abomination.lore: Similar to the spell wraith, this monster is what remains of some long-forgotten research project. Something must have gone terribly wrong with it.
exp_enemy.lab_abomination.name: Lab Abomination
exp_enemy.mirror_shade.lore: Shades equipped with silver mirrors, reflecting some magic back at the colonists.
exp_enemy.mirror_shade.name: Mirror Shade
exp_enemy.mirror_twin.lore: Reflections of our colonists and the allies we've made over the years. They're always found on the ceiling, so don't forget to look up.
exp_enemy.mirror_twin.name: Mirror Twin
exp_enemy.oblivion_spawn.lore: A giant bipedal roach that creeps through the deepest parts of the void. It seems to share a close connection to the void and shows its cunning through ambush tactics.
exp_enemy.oblivion_spawn.name: Oblivion Spawn
exp_enemy.palace_champion.lore: A skilled member of the palace guard, loyal only to the king himself. The best of the best in terms of martial prowess.
exp_enemy.palace_champion.name: Palace Champion
exp_enemy.penitent_guardian.lore: Similar to their penitent kin, these guardians are under strict contract. They act as the enforcers of pacts, ensuring debtors have no escape until their debts are paid in full.
exp_enemy.penitent_guardian.name: Penitent Guardian
exp_enemy.reality_shred.lore: Flying fish that seem to feed on order. They seem to grow in power every time a colonist asks how they breathe out of water.
exp_enemy.reality_shred.name: Reality Shred
exp_enemy.runite_elemental.lore: An elemental bound to the caverns. They greatly resemble the mining golems, making you wonder if the miners based their designs on these denizens.
exp_enemy.runite_elemental.name: Runite Elemental
exp_enemy.shade.lore: A ghostly presence that haunts the explorers of the void. It leeches energy from living things and should be dealt with quickly whenever encountered.
exp_enemy.shade.name: Shade
exp_enemy.shade_wraith.lore: Similar to the Shades seen in other realms, but a lot more persistent. They too drain life from all living things around them, with their hunger appearing to be insatiable.
exp_enemy.shade_wraith.name: Shade Wraith
exp_enemy.shadow_imp.lore: An impish creature that may be mistaken for a Kobaloi at a distance. Up close it becomes far more obvious that this thing is made entirely of some dark substance that completely absorbs the light.
exp_enemy.shadow_imp.name: Shadow Imp
exp_enemy.shard_spider.lore: A giant spider covered in scales of crystal. These are often seen skittering on the ceiling of the caverns.
exp_enemy.shard_spider.name: Shard Spider
exp_enemy.shifting_horror.lore: Monsters that take the appearance of many of our colony's enemies throughout the years.
exp_enemy.shifting_horror.name: Shifting Horror
exp_enemy.spell_wraith.lore: A creature made from the remnants of a spell cast a long time ago. It seems to haunt the space it once supported as a magical helper.
exp_enemy.spell_wraith.name: Spell Wraith
exp_enemy.spore_walker.lore: A plant creature infected by blight. It moves much faster than its creeping kin.
exp_enemy.spore_walker.name: Spore Walker
exp_enemy.thorn_beast.lore: A jungle predator covered in sharp thorns. Its teeth are even sharper.
exp_enemy.thorn_beast.name: Thorn Beast
exp_enemy.tome_guardian.lore: A floating eyeball that diligently guards the quiet library's books. It is unclear just how long these beings have served as protectors.
exp_enemy.tome_guardian.name: Tome Guardian
exp_enemy.vine_creeper.lore: A slow-moving plant creature that creeps along the canopy above.
exp_enemy.vine_creeper.name: Vine Creeper

exp_enemy.void_broker.name: Void Broker
exp_enemy.void_herald.lore: Heralds of the Void Arbiter, blessed with their own pacts with the lowly penitents. These advanced guardians act directly under the command of their Arbiter.
exp_enemy.void_herald.name: Void Herald
exp_enemy.void_horror.lore: A large-mouthed monster that swims through the abyssal sea like a deep-water fish. Its teeth are long and sharp and its eyes shine brightly in the dark of the abyss.
exp_enemy.void_horror.name: Abyss Horror
exp_enemy.void_penitent.lore: Unrecognizable beings that have been trapped here after taking bad deals. They will likely never be able to pay their dues, remaining servants to the Arbiter for the rest of their days.
exp_enemy.void_penitent.name: Void Penitent
exp_enemy.void_stalker.lore: A strange eyeball with a piercing stare. It stands tall on a pitch-black eyestalk, much like that of a crab. Despite all of the oddities, the eyeball itself looks far too human.
exp_enemy.void_stalker.name: Abyss Stalker

glossary.building_resources.construction: While in Build mode you can right-click in the game world to deconstruct buildings and recover a portion of their materials. You can also press X from Build mode to toggle Destruction mode. This is useful for reorganizing your colony layout as you expand. Colonists with Building skill handle destruction tasks. Right-clicking a chest inside an ancient crypt marks it for looting instead.
Press B to enter Build mode, select a building, and place it on valid terrain. Colonists with building priority will construct it using resources from the stockpile.
Many advanced buildings require specific research to unlock. Hover over locked buildings in the build menu to see their prerequisites, or browse the research tree to plan ahead.
Each building requires specific resources. Costs are shown in the build menu before placement and are taken from the stockpile automatically when queued.

Place floors inside walled areas to create rooms. A room needs walls on all sides, at least one door, and floor tiles inside. Rooms provide quality-based bonuses to sleeping, crafting, or socializing based on the room's furnishings.

Walls, doors, and fences have health points. Enemies with no clear path to their target must break through these buildings by attacking them. Damaged structures automatically queue repair tasks when threats are gone.
glossary.building_resources.resources.fo: Food spoils over time. Decay is faster in summer and slower in winter. Build Food Chests and Ice Boxes to reduce spoilage rates and keep your food supply stable.
glossary.building_resources.resources.ga: Press G to designate trees for chopping (yields wood) and rock deposits for mining (yields stone, iron ore, or runite). Colonists with Building skill handle gathering tasks.
glossary.building_resources.resources.gl: All resources are colony-wide and instantly accessible. There is no hauling: colonists use materials directly from the shared stockpile when working.
glossary.building_resources.resources.pr: Raw materials can be refined into advanced forms: wood into planks, stone into bricks, hides into leather, iron ore into iron. These are often needed for mid-to-late-game recipes, so be sure to keep a stockpile of each refined material.
glossary.building_resources.title: Building & Resources
glossary.colonists_needs.colony_populati: You start with room for 3 colonists. Each colony milestone you reach raises the cap: +1 on small worlds, +1.5 on medium and +2 on large, for a maximum of 12, 16 and 21. Milestones are a mix of surviving Void Nexus waves and conquering realm chain expeditions, so reaching the maximum takes progress in both.

The milestones are: (1) Survive wave 1, (2) Complete any Tier 1 realm expedition, (3) Survive wave 3, (4) Complete any Tier 2 realm expedition, (5) Defeat a full realm chain boss, (6) Survive wave 6, (7) Conquer two full realm chains, (8) Survive wave 9, (9) Conquer three full realm chains. The Rifts panel hints at the next one in this order, but you are free to complete them in any order.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.crit: Automatic warnings appear when colonists are near starvation, approaching a mental break, or freezing in cold weather.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.hung: Decays over time. Colonists interrupt work to eat when critically hungry. Cooked food fully restores hunger whereas raw food only partially restores it.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.ment: When mood drops critically low, colonists enter a breaking state. While in this state the colonist will wander aimlessly and refuse tasks until their mood recovers.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.mood: A colonist's mood is their base value modified by active thoughts. Mood level directly determines work speed and willingness to work.
Four tiers from best to worst: Inspired (fastest work), Content (normal speed), Stressed (slow), and Breaking (refuses all work). Keep colonists above the stress threshold for productive labor.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.rest: Decays over time. Colonists seek sleep when exhausted. Sleeping in an assigned bed gives a mood bonus while sleeping on the ground does not.
glossary.colonists_needs.needs_mood.thou: Temporary mood modifiers gained from events, meal quality, weather, social interactions, achievements, and room quality. Each thought fades after a duration.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.bufos.tex: Cold-blooded creatures who work faster during the day and slower at night. They also tend to tire more slowly than other races.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.ferin.tex: Nature-bonded beings with a bonus to farming speed and exceptional skill with animals. They tend to get restless when stuck indoors for too long.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.human.tex: Versatile generalists who learn all skills, both mundane and magical, faster than other races.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.kobalos.t: Pack-minded workers who move faster and grow tougher when surrounded by allies, but they become rattled when alone. Additionally, they suffer no mood penalty from eating raw food.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.nymph.tex: Magically attuned beings who gain magic skill experience much faster than other races, but are physically frail and work more slowly.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.races_ove: Five playable races, each with a unique racial trait that provides passive bonuses. Colonists of all races work together and can fill any role.
glossary.colonists_needs.races.subtitle: Races
glossary.colonists_needs.skills_health.a: Temporary buffs from potions and spells appear in the colonist info panel with remaining duration. Effects include speed boosts, damage shields, and healing. Buffed colonists pulse on the map.
glossary.colonists_needs.skills_health.e: Each colonist has Weapon, Armor, Helmet, Clothes, Boots, Tool, and Trinket slots. Use Auto-equip to quickly assign the best available gear, or manually equip from the inventory.
glossary.colonists_needs.skills_health.h: Colonists have hit points that regenerate slowly when idle and faster when sleeping. If a colonist dies, surviving colonists suffer severe mood penalties based on their relationship.
glossary.colonists_needs.skills_health.s: Skills improve through use, with completing related tasks granting experience. Each level requires progressively more experience than the last.
Six work skills (Building, Farming, Crafting, Cooking, Animals, Research) plus six magic schools. Higher skill levels mean faster task completion and better outcomes.
glossary.colonists_needs.title: Colonists & Needs
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.animal_t: Beast Whisperer (better taming and animal handling), Menagerist (cheered by nearby tamed animals), Skittish (worse at taming). These affect interactions with wildlife and tamed creatures.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.combat_t: Duelist (dodge chance), Deadeye (critical hit chance), Berserker (stronger at low health), Coward (flees early), Pacifist (refuses combat). These traits directly affect performance in battle.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.expediti: Trailblazer, Treasure Hunter, Trapsmith, Inspiring, Void-Touched, Night Owl, Green Thumb (certain traits can also have realm-specific bonuses on expeditions). These traits give bonuses during expeditions such as reduced duration, better loot, or party-wide buffs.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.food_tra: Gourmand (strong reaction to meal quality), Foraging Gut (no penalty from raw food), Chef (better cooking output), Comfort Eater (eating restores extra mood). These affect how colonists interact with food and hunger.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.magic_tr: Attuned (bonus mana regen and max mana), Spellsword (bonus spell damage), Magically Inept (much slower magic XP but slightly faster mundane XP). These affect a colonist's relationship with spellcasting.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.rare_tra: Lucky (better crafting quality on all items), Prodigy (gains all XP faster), Magically Gifted (starts with experience in a random magic school and its starter spell). These are uncommon to very rare and have powerful effects.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.social_t: Socialite, Loner, Optimist, Pessimist, Charismatic, Abrasive, Loyal. These affect mood from social interactions, thought intensity, and how quickly relationships form or sour.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.subtitle: Traits
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.survival: Iron Stomach, Gluttonous, Tough, Brave, Quick, Sturdy, Light Sleeper, Deep Sleeper, Steadfast, Volatile. These modify hunger/rest decay, damage resistance, movement speed, or mental resilience.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.trade_tr: Silver Tongue (better trade prices), Merchant's Eye (Trade Rift rewards arrive at higher quality), Scavenger (chance to find bonus materials while gathering).
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.traits_o: Permanent modifiers assigned when a colonist is created. Each colonist gets one to three traits. Some trait pairs are mutually exclusive.
glossary.colonists_needs.traits.work_tra: Hard Worker, Lazy, Night Owl, Early Bird, Creative, Scholar, Workaholic, Insomniac. These affect work speed, skill growth rate, or time-of-day performance.
glossary.combat_exploration.ancient_cryp: Sealed, door-less tombs scattered across the map, some round and some square. Their interior stays dark and unexplored until a wall is broken. Seven crypts hold a rift anchor, one for each realm chain beyond the Wild Frontiers, and each sits in the biome that suits its realm. Larger maps also hold extra crypts with loot only. Crypts you have discovered show on the minimap as their realm chain icon on a coloured disc: purple while sealed, blue while warded, red once breached and green once plundered.

Deconstruct any wall of a crypt's outer ring in Build mode (right-click, or X for Deconstruct mode). The moment the ring is open the crypt wakes: its guardians rise and its traps arm, so bring armed colonists. The sealed interior cannot be entered, built on or designated until then. Ordinary ruins and the ruins that hold Arcane Cores are never sealed or guarded.

In Build mode, right-click a chest to mark it for looting (the same way you deconstruct a wall) and a colonist will open it. Contents depend on the crypt's tier and include materials from its realm. A crypt counts as plundered once every chest is looted.

Breaching a crypt wakes guardians themed to its realm. They chase colonists who come within range and return to their post when nothing is near. Deeper crypts have tougher guardians. Hidden spike traps lie on the floor and hurt the first colonist to step on each one. A trap, once sprung, is spent.

Each anchor crypt is dressed for its realm. Verdant: forest, wooden walls, briar guardians. Crystal: mountains, stone walls, crystal guardians. Arcane: grassland, brick walls, rune constructs. Shadow: swamp, stone walls, shades. Void Pact: tundra, void walls, void servants. Chaos: desert, brick walls, fracture horrors. Kingdom: grassland, stone and brick, risen palace guards.

Some crypts are warded. Their walls are indestructible warded stone (▦) until the realm chain they are bound to has been completed by clearing its final boss realm. Verdant and Crystal crypts are always open. After that the order is Arcane (after Crystal), Shadow (after Arcane), Void Pact (after Shadow), Kingdom (after Void Pact) and Chaos (after Kingdom). Loot-only crypts follow the same rule: tier 2 after Crystal and tier 3 after Void Pact. You are notified when a ward fades, and discovering a warded crypt tells you what to clear.

Each anchor crypt holds a dormant rift anchor (✧). Once the crypt is open, right-click the anchor in Build mode to have a colonist attune it (✦), or right-click it with colonists drafted to send them straight there. Crypt chests work the same way. An attuned anchor is the portal for its realm chain: parties gather there, depart from it and return to it. Launching also needs Planar Rifts research, and each realm keeps its own research and prerequisite requirements. The Wild Frontiers need no anchor. Worlds created before anchors existed use the Rift Gate instead.
glossary.combat_exploration.combat.armor: Body armor and helmets reduce incoming damage. Heavier armor provides more protection in exchange for fewer magical bonuses. The two slots stack together for combined damage reduction.
glossary.combat_exploration.combat.draft: Press Q to draft selected colonists for manual control. Drafted colonists ignore all tasks, including eating and sleeping, and move where you right-click. Box-select multiple colonists and Draft All for group control.
glossary.combat_exploration.combat.how_c: Melee weapons attack adjacent tiles whereas ranged weapons and spells attack from a distance (with the exception of melee spells like Smite). Colonists engage in battle with enemies that step too close, automatically attacking any threat within their weapon range.
glossary.combat_exploration.combat.weapo: Three categories: Melee (swords, daggers, axes, and maces, all close range with varying attack speeds), Ranged (bows and crossbows for attacking from distance), and Magic (wands and staves for boosting spell damage and attacking at range). Higher-tier weapons within each category deal more damage or have better bonuses.
glossary.combat_exploration.defense.defe: Use walls and doors to funnel enemies through chokepoints. Place turrets along the path they must take. Reinforce critical walls with higher-tier materials (Void Walls) for durability.
glossary.combat_exploration.defense.guar: Assign colonists to guard a position. They patrol nearby and automatically engage threats within a wider radius than normal, while still eating and sleeping when needed.
glossary.combat_exploration.defense.peac: A game setting that disables raids and hostile wildlife. The Void Nexus wave system still functions separately for players who want optional combat challenges.
glossary.combat_exploration.defense.raid: Hostile raiders attack your colony periodically. Raid strength scales with your colony's wealth and how long you've been playing. Disabled in Peaceful Mode.
glossary.combat_exploration.defense.turr: Arcane Sentinels and Void Turrets automatically attack enemies within range. Inferno Wards and Ember Heaters damage or deter nearby hostiles. All defensive buildings consume mana from the grid.
Research the Auto-Expedition tech chain to allow saved party presets to embark automatically when all members are rested and ready. Higher tiers of the research allow more presets to run simultaneously, enabling hands-off farming of multiple realms at once.

During expeditions, your party faces combat encounters, traps, and discoveries. Combat resolves in real-time rounds. Even on defeat, you keep items found before the loss. Colonists defeated during an expedition will always survive their retreat, re-joining the colony at extremely low health.

After returning from an expedition, colonists enter a rest period before they can embark again. Longer or harder expeditions impose longer fatigue. The Trailblazer trait and certain expedition XP level bonuses reduce fatigue duration.
Select up to five colonists, two pack animals, and two war beasts. Choose a realm and difficulty level. Higher difficulty means tougher enemies but significantly better loot and rare item chances.

Colonists earn expedition experience each time they complete a run. As they level up they unlock passive bonuses: increased damage, better loot, reduced fatigue, and higher rare encounter rates. Expedition level is tracked per-colonist and persists across all realms.

When building an expedition party, assign colonists to the front or back row. Front-row fighters absorb more incoming attacks while back-row members benefit from cover. Placing your toughest warriors up front and your spellcasters or archers in the back is generally the most effective approach.

Tamed okapi can join expeditions as pack animals, reducing expedition duration. Bring them for faster completion and more efficient loot runs. Pack animals do not participate in combat and always return home safely.

Save your favorite party configurations as named presets from the expedition panel. Presets store the colonist lineup, formation, and carried potions, letting you quickly re-field a proven team without rebuilding it each time.

Colonists who share a strong relationship fight better together. Friends, close friends, and lovers in the same expedition party gain a damage bonus, while rivals and adversaries in the party can undercut each other. The relationship thoughts you invest in at home carry real weight in the field.

Multiple expedition chains, each with increasing depth. Deeper realms require completing the previous one first. Later chains require additional research to unlock. Except for the Wild Frontiers, a chain can only be launched once you have researched Planar Rifts and attuned its rift anchor in an ancient crypt.

A legacy launch point. In worlds where every realm chain has a rift anchor (every new world) the Rift Gate can no longer be built and expeditions leave from attuned Rift Anchors instead (see Ancient Crypts). Worlds created before anchors existed keep using the gate: build it after researching Planar Rifts, click it to open the expedition panel, and send parties to other realms for loot.

Tamed wolves and boars can join expeditions as war beasts, fighting alongside your party in combat encounters. Unlike pack animals, war beasts actively participate in battle and can take damage. They always return home safely even if the party is defeated.
glossary.combat_exploration.title: Combat & Exploration
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.dur: Certain powerful trinkets break after activating their effect. Broken trinkets provide no bonuses. Repair tasks take place at an Anvil using runite and are queued automatically.
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.equ: When worn by a colonist, these provide passive bonuses: increased move speed, work speed, combat power, or emergency auto-revival. Some have special expedition-only effects.
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.fin: Found as expedition loot (each realm chain has signature drops), purchased from rare trader inventories, or occasionally crafted with end-game research and materials.
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.ped: Pour extra mana into a pedestal from its info panel. Empowered costs 2x mana for 1.5x effects and +2 radius. Radiant costs 3x mana for 2x effects and +4 radius. Whole-number bonuses like extra harvest yield gain +1 or +2 instead. Colony-wide trinkets can only be Empowered.
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.tri: Build after researching Arcane Infusion. Place a trinket on a pedestal to project its effect in a radius around it. Some trinkets have global effects that benefit the entire colony. Pedestals consume mana based on the placed trinket.
glossary.combat_exploration.trinkets.wha: Powerful unique items with special effects. Some are equipped directly on colonists for personal bonuses while others are placed on Trinket Pedestals to project area or colony-wide effects.
glossary.combat_exploration.wave_defense: Each successive wave sends tougher and more numerous enemies. Defeat all enemies in a wave to complete it and unlock the next. Waves are strictly player-initiated, not automatic.

Build walls and doors to create funnels toward the Nexus. Place turrets at chokepoints. Draft your colonists or set them to Guard mode to protect the Nexus themselves. Upgrade weapons and armor between waves.
Dropped by wave enemies. This rare resource is essential for crafting late-game equipment and advanced defensive structures.

Build after researching Unstable Rifts. You can start wave challenges using the Rifts menu (V). During a wave enemies spawn from portals and try to destroy the Nexus. Defend it from these attacks to earn rewards. Don't worry: if your Nexus is destroyed you can always build a new one to replace it.
glossary.crafting_production.cooking_pot: Convert raw crops and meat into cooked meals at the Cooking Pot. Cooked food fully restores hunger and provides a mood bonus. Eating raw food gives a mood penalty instead.
Crops from farming, meat from hunting animals, and products from tamed creatures (eggs, milk) all serve as cooking ingredients.

Brewed at the Alchemy Table after researching Alchemy. Potions provide temporary buffs like healing, speed, mana restoration, or damage resistance. They are auto-consumed when trigger conditions are met.
glossary.crafting_production.crafting_sy: Set stock targets on recipes to automatically queue them when supplies run low. Toggle repeat mode to keep a recipe permanently queued. Great for maintaining food and potion supplies as well as keeping materials stocked.

Different items require different stations: a Workbench for basic goods, an Anvil for metalwork, a Cooking Pot for cooking, an Alchemy Table for potions, an Enchanting Table for enchantments and runic gear, a Loom for clothing, and a Scriptorium for crafting spell tomes. Build the right station, then queue recipes. Building multiple of the same workstation will allow more colonists to take on crafting tasks at the unoccupied stations.

Similar to equipment Quality, you can choose to enchant any non-trinket equipment from the inventory for a small cost. This will queue an enchantment task that is prioritized as a crafting task but distinctly uses the Enchantment skill level from the working colonist. These enchantments vary widely, applying some new effect to the equipment with a power level based on the enchantment's tier (I, II, III, or IV). The higher the Enchantment skill, the better the odds of higher enchantment tiers. Enchanted equipment can also be queued for enchantment multiple times, replacing the previous effect with a newly rolled one, allowing you to re-enchant your best equipment until you find an effect that you're satisfied with.

Open the Craft panel (C) and queue recipes. Colonists with Crafting or Cooking skill will work queued recipes at the appropriate station. Mana-powered stations (Enchanting Tables) work faster than their unpowered counterparts (Workbenches).

Crafted equipment rolls a quality level from Crude to Superior. Higher Crafting skill gives that colonist better odds of higher quality crafts. Quality multiplies the item's effectiveness significantly, with high-quality equipment from lower tiers outpacing low-quality equipment from higher tiers.
Recycle unwanted equipment from the inventory to recover a portion of its crafting materials. Useful for clearing out low-quality gear after upgrades.
glossary.crafting_production.title: Crafting & Production
glossary.crafting_production.trading.exc: Some powerful items cannot be crafted and are only available from traders or as expedition loot. Watch for rare offerings when caravans arrive.
glossary.crafting_production.trading.mer: Different merchants carry different goods. Arms Dealers sell weapons and armor. Tome Peddlers sell spell tomes. Wandering Alchemists sell potions and rare ingredients. Clothiers sell clothing and boots. Expedition Outfitters carry expedition supplies and pack-animal gear. Rare Goods Brokers stock late-game trinkets and exotic materials. Watch for rare offerings when caravans arrive.
glossary.crafting_production.trading.tra: Merchants arrive as random events. Open the barter panel to exchange resources and items. You sell at a discount and buy at a markup compared to base values.
Research Trade Routes to improve your buy and sell rates colony-wide, making trading significantly more efficient.

An advanced building unlocked with Trade Rifts research. It presents periodic supply contracts: fulfill the requested goods within the season (or year, for larger contracts) to earn high-quality equipment, spell tomes, or rare artifacts. Seasonal contracts refresh each season while yearly contracts refresh once per year and carry bigger rewards. The quality floor on received gear is higher than what you tend to see when crafting, making the Trade Rift one of the best sources of top-tier equipment.
glossary.relationships_social.social_sys: Random social events occur when colonists work or idle nearby: pleasant chats, shared meals, disagreements, and arguments. The more time colonists spend with each other, the more they will learn to enjoy the company.
A hidden score between any two colonists ranging from very negative to very positive. This score shifts from social interactions and slowly decays toward neutral over time.
Progresses from Stranger through Acquaintance, Friend, and Close Friend, up to Lovers. Can also go negative to Rival and Adversary. Higher tiers provide stronger mood effects.
Colonists near each other periodically interact. Each interaction shifts their opinion of each other, determining their shared relationship tier.
Making friends, falling in love, or losing loved ones to death all cause powerful mood effects. Relationship-based thoughts are among the strongest in the game.
Socialite colonists interact more often and gain mood from company. Loners prefer solitude and get stressed when crowded. Optimists amplify positive social thoughts. Pessimists amplify negative ones.
glossary.relationships_social.title: Relationships & Social

glossary.research_magic.golems.creating_: Build a Golem Forge (requires Golem Craft research) and craft golems using stone, runite, and void essence. Multiple types available, each specializing in a different skill.
glossary.research_magic.golems.golem_lim: Golems cannot learn spells, cannot grow in skill, and do not count toward your colonist cap. They are pure task specialists, reliable but inflexible.
glossary.research_magic.golems.subtitle: Golems
glossary.research_magic.golems.what_are_: Animated stone workers that never eat, sleep, or have mood. Each golem specializes in one task type and works tirelessly without any needs management.
glossary.research_magic.magic_system.aut: Colonists auto-cast known spells when appropriate conditions are met (healing when allies are hurt, buffing speed when working). Each colonist attunes to one magic school at a time and auto-casts spells from that school only. Switching is free. Disable specific spells to conserve mana for higher-priority casts.
glossary.research_magic.magic_system.col: Each colonist has a personal mana pool that grows as they level magic skills. Spells consume mana and go on cooldown. Mana regenerates passively over time or can be restored instantly via potions.
glossary.research_magic.magic_system.div: {summary} Colonists with Divination skill also generate Omens: prophecies visible in the Arcane panel (V) that give advance warning of incoming raids, weather shifts, and events. Higher Divination skill reveals finer timing and unlocks more omen categories, including hints about what lurks in expedition realms.
glossary.research_magic.magic_system.lea: Colonists learn spells by studying Spell Tomes at a Research Desk, prioritized by the Research skill. Each tome teaches one spell. Progress persists per-colonist, and completing a tome permanently grants that spell, destroying the tome in the process. Colonists will slowly study their tome while contributing to research topic progress. Colonists will study their tome at a faster pace if there's no research topic to contribute to.
glossary.research_magic.magic_system.mag: Six schools of magic, each with a distinct role: Evocation (damage), Enchantment (buffs and crowd control), Abjuration (healing and shields), Conjuration (summons and teleportation), Transmutation (crop growth and terrain manipulation), Divination (influencing fate and events).
Your primary power source. You start with a limited build cap that increases through research and rare consumables. Each crystal generates a base amount of mana for the grid.
Reduce mana consumption of nearby buildings. Place relays in clusters of powered buildings to stretch your mana budget further. The reduction does not stack from multiple relays.

Mana Crystals generate power while magical buildings and pedestals consume it. If demand exceeds generation, the grid powers buildings in priority order and the rest go dark until supply catches up. The mana display shows net mana and how many buildings are dark.
Balance generation versus consumption as you add powered buildings.

Every mana consumer has a priority: High, Normal or Low. When mana runs short, High is supplied first, then Normal, then Low. Defenses and heaters default to High, lights to Low, everything else to Normal. Change a building's priority from its info panel (the default is marked with *). Mana Relays always draw first.
glossary.research_magic.research.how_res: Select a topic from the research tree, then colonists study at Research Desks to progress it. Only one active project at a time. Additional desks contribute with diminishing returns.
glossary.research_magic.research.researc: Advanced technologies may require more than just a prerequisite tech. Some need specific buildings on the map, population milestones, or a minimum number of completed techs in their tab.

The tree is organized into multiple tabs covering different progression paths: foundations, nature, arcane power, crafting, advanced magic, and void/exploration. Cross-tab prerequisites exist between them.
glossary.research_magic.research.what_re: New buildings, recipes, crops, spells, and capabilities. Browse the tree early to plan your progression path. Some powerful buildings and mechanics are locked behind multi-step research chains.
glossary.research_magic.title: Research & Magic
glossary.work_tasks.room_workshop_qualit: Enclosed bedrooms (walls + door + floor + bed) have a quality score based on furnishings and decorations inside. Better bedrooms give a bigger mood bonus when colonists sleep there. Ideal size is 6–12 tiles per bed. Requires 1 Seating, 1 Table / Desk, and 1 Storage to rise above Comfortable.

Each furnishing counts as a type: Seating (chair, stool, bench, armchair), Table / Desk (table, nightstand, desk), Storage (shelf, bookcase, wardrobe, material shelf, crate), Tools (tool rack, weapon rack, grindstone), or Centerpiece (podium, statue, war table). A piece only meets a requirement in rooms it improves. Misc pieces (potted plant, personal chest, painting, tapestry) add decoration but never meet a requirement. Click a room to see what it still needs.

Place a Town Hall Banner in a furnished room to designate it as a gathering space. Idle colonists spend time here to socialize and get mood boosts. Better decorations improve the effect. Ideal size is 13–30 tiles. Requires 4 Seating, 1 Table / Desk, and 1 Centerpiece to become Majestic.

Crafting stations in furnished rooms gain speed and quality bonuses. Nearby tool racks, chairs, tables, and material shelves all improve workshop effectiveness. Ideal size is 8–15 tiles per station. Requires 1 Tools, 1 Storage, and 1 Seating to rise above Professional.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.how_task: When you designate work (building, gathering, farming, etc.), tasks enter a queue. Colonists pick tasks based on their priority settings for the relevant skill.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.idle_beh: Colonists with no tasks may wander, stargaze, skip stones, or socialize. If a Town Hall exists, idle colonists will gather there for mood-boosting relaxation activities.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.mood_wor: Inspired colonists work noticeably faster. Stressed colonists work significantly slower. Breaking colonists stop working entirely until their mood recovers.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.prioriti: Set each skill from 1 (highest priority) to 5 (lowest), or disable it entirely. Colonists always attempt the lowest-numbered available task they have skill for, nearest first. To jump one order ahead of the rest (say, a crypt wall far from home), right-click it in Normal mode with nobody drafted to mark it Do First.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.subtitle: Task System
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.tool_bon: Equipping the right tool type (Pickaxe, Axe, Sickle, Hammer, Mattock) speeds up matching tasks. Higher-tier tools provide bigger bonuses. Mattocks cover multiple tasks but are weaker than specialists. The Tool slot also accepts off-hand combat items like shields and quivers, as well as utility items like lanterns and war drums.
glossary.work_tasks.task_system.work_spe: How fast a colonist completes tasks is determined by their skill level, mood, traits, equipped tool, active spell or trinket effects, and workshop quality. All bonuses multiply together.
glossary.work_tasks.title: Work & Tasks
WASD or Arrow keys to pan. +/- or scroll wheel to zoom. Middle-click drag to pan. Home to center on selection.
glossary.world_controls.controls.combat_: Q drafts/undrafts selected colonists. Right-click moves drafted colonists. Number keys 1-9 cast the selected colonist's controllable spells.
glossary.world_controls.controls.keybind: All keys can be remapped in Settings under Controls / Keybindings.
glossary.world_controls.controls.modes.t: B for Build mode, F for Farm Zone mode, G for Gather/Designate mode. X toggles deconstruct while in Build mode.
glossary.world_controls.controls.overlay: H = Warmth (heat source radii). Y = Defense (turret and ward attack ranges). U = Room Quality (rooms colored by tier: blue = bare, green = mid, gold = best). K = Auras (mana relay discount zones, pedestal artifact radii, light source radii).
P (Priority), C (Craft), R (Research), I (Inventory), V (Arcane), J (Story). Esc closes any open panel.
glossary.world_controls.controls.pause_s: Space to pause/unpause. {slower_key} and {faster_key} to change game speed (three levels). [ and ] to cycle between colonists.
glossary.world_controls.controls.selecti: Click to select a colonist, animal, or tile. Drag to box-select multiple. E selects all colonists. N jumps to next idle colonist.
glossary.world_controls.events.destructi: Creeping miasma infects and decays crops in spring/summer. Blight blooms erupt on crops and destroy them in summer/autumn. Cold snaps kill all outdoor crops in winter.
glossary.world_controls.events.random_ev: Various events trigger as your colony grows: new colonists arriving, trade caravans, crop blights, mineral windfalls, cold snaps, animal migrations, and inspiration.
glossary.world_controls.events.subtitle: Events
glossary.world_controls.events.wanderers: New colonists occasionally ask to join your colony. Wanderers are more likely when colony mood is high. Accept or reject based on their traits and skills. Once a wanderer joins your colony you will have no simple way to remove them from their new community.
glossary.world_controls.farming.availabl: Crops range from basic (available immediately) to advanced (requiring research). Each has different season compatibility, growth speed, and yield. Some crops, like the magical Moonbloom, grow in all seasons.
glossary.world_controls.farming.blight_b: Hostile fungal entities that erupt on crop tiles in summer and autumn, destroying nearby crops rapidly. Must be killed by colonists in combat. The Seedkeeper's Locket passively damages blooms within its aura. Ward of Calamity prevents blooms from spawning.
glossary.world_controls.farming.creeping: A blight that infects crop tiles in spring and summer, causing growth to decay. Spreads to adjacent crops over time. Farmers can cleanse infected tiles. Blight Ward potions double cleanse speed. Pedestal artifacts like the Seedkeeper's Locket create immunity zones.
glossary.world_controls.farming.crop_gro: Growth speed is affected by the current season, weather conditions, and magic spells. By default most crops do not grow during the winter season.
glossary.world_controls.farming.farm_zon: Press F to enter Farm Zone mode. Select a crop type, then drag an area on grass or dirt. Colonists with Farming skill will automatically plant and harvest crops in the zone.
glossary.world_controls.farming.subtitle: Farming
Cooling temperatures with slightly slower crop growth. Animal migrations commonly pass through, providing hunting opportunities.
Four seasons rotate continuously: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter. Each season affects temperature, crop growth rates, animal spawns, and which events can occur.
Moderate temperatures and normal crop growth. Wild animals appear more frequently. A good season for expanding farms and taming animals.
The hottest season with the fastest crop growth, but food also spoils faster. Risk of heat waves. Plan extra food storage.
Rain boosts crop growth. Blizzards halt all crop growth entirely. Weather varies by season.

Cold temperatures halt most outdoor crop growth. Snow covers the ground. Colonists need warmth from Campfires, Ember Heaters, or Inferno Wards to avoid freezing. Freezing colonists will seek out nearby heat sources on their own. Press H to toggle the warmth overlay and see each source's coverage.

Once each year, when winter arrives, the colony holds a feast if it has stored a comfortable surplus of food. The feast eats into that stockpile and grants every colonist a lasting mood buff, a warm beat in the coldest season. A lean winter with too little food stored simply passes without one, so keep a cushion of food heading into the cold.
glossary.world_controls.title: World & Controls
Some animals (wolves) fight back when taming fails. The colonist takes damage and gains negative mood. Higher Animals skill reduces failure risk.
Select an animal and click Hunt to queue a hunting task. Colonists with Animals skill will pursue it and attack when able. Hunting yields meat and hides for cooking and crafting.

Tamed animals serve different purposes: guard animals patrol and attack threats, pack animals speed up expeditions, production animals generate resources like eggs, and some rare animals even provide passive mood auras to nearby colonists.
Build a Beast Circle (requires Beast Binding research) to tame wild animals. Taming requires food and Animals skill. Higher skill improves success chance.
Various creatures roam the map. Passive animals (deer, rabbits, okapi) flee when approached. Hostile animals (wolves) attack colonists that get too close, especially at night and in winter.

magic_skill.abjuration.summary: Healing, cleansing and shields. Mends wounded allies at home and in combat. On expeditions, Shield guards whoever enemies target most, and Guardian Ward covers the whole party.
magic_skill.conjuration.name: Conjuration
magic_skill.conjuration.summary: Summons that fight beside your colonists (familiars, ghosts, wisps and monsters), decoys that draw enemy attacks, and short-range teleports. An expedition party can have up to 3 summons at once, and summons grow stronger with Conjuration level.

magic_skill.evocation.summary: Damage spells: bolts, fireballs and chain lightning that strike enemies at range, in raids and on expeditions. They hit harder as the caster's Evocation level rises.

magic_skill.transmutation.summary: Colony magic that speeds crop growth, enriches soil, shapes stone and terrain, and transmutes materials. Little use on expeditions.

npc.trapped_miner.lore: A miner who has been trapped in a cave-in within the crystal mines. They seem to be unrelated to the ancient miners that built the tunnels, but they have a good knowledge of the veins and passages in the mines. They are grateful for any help, sharing their knowledge or battling alongside our colonists for a time. They seem to always disappear after being rescued, often muttering about a shortcut home that they know. The colonists suspect that the miner must live somewhere inside the caverns and has no interest in leaving any time soon.
npc.trapped_miner.name: Trapped Miner
npc.trapped_miner.text: A muffled voice calls from behind a cave-in. A miner, pinned but alive.

realm.ancient_university.events.rare.1.t: {name} finds an enchanted runite cache in the alchemy wing!
realm.ancient_university.events.rare.2.t: {name} finds a set of spectacles that reveal hidden truths!
realm.ancient_university.events.rare.3.t: {name} discovers a shared wisdom codex in the Dean's private study!
realm.ancient_university.events.traps.0: A failed experiment reactivates as {name} passes, explosion!
realm.ancient_university.events.traps.1: {name} triggers a student's old ward, and lightning arcs!
realm.ancient_university.events.traps.2: An animated suit of armor swings at {name}!
realm.ancient_university.events.traps.3: A containment circle breaks, releasing stored energy at {name}!
realm.ancient_university.name: Ancient University
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.approach: A half-finished golem whirrs to life, crackling with unstable magic!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.defeatTe: The Arcane Construct overloads and detonates in a shower of sparks!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.lore: A sentient construct born through magical experimentation. One of the few surviving research notes makes mention of the being's peaceful nature and gentleness. It is of little surprise that all of these years alone would send it into madness.
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.name: The Arcane Construct
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.phases.0: Arcane shielding deflects much of your damage!
The Arcane Construct accelerates! Sparks fly wildly!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.phases.1: Absorbed magic discharges in a shockwave!
The Construct's arcane shell is beginning to crack!
The Construct absorbs ambient magic, warping the air around it!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.phases.2: Arcane bolts discharge in every direction!
Flickering shields still resist some blows!
The Construct begins to destabilize! Raw energy leaks from its core!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.boss.phases.3: The Construct erupts in a cascade of unstable magic!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.ambien: {name} passes containment chambers. Most are cracked and empty.
Unstable magical fields distort the air like heat shimmer.
{name} reads warning signs in a dozen languages on every door.
A half-finished construct twitches as the party passes.
Arcane waste pools glow an unsettling green in side chambers.
{name} hears the hum of a still-running experiment deep below.
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.discov: {name} finds an intact experimental prototype in a sealed chamber.
A researcher's emergency stash, hidden for a quick escape that never came.
{name} recovers usable materials from a decommissioned experiment.
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.rare.0: {name} accesses the head researcher's personal vault, forbidden knowledge!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.rare.1: {name} finds concentrated void essence in a sealed containment jar!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.rare.2: {name} recovers a pair of spectacles from a researcher's cluttered desk, lenses still intact!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.rare.3: {name} discovers a soulbound scepter in a sealed experiment chamber, its spirit-link still active!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.events.rare.4: {name} finds a condensed field spellbook in a researcher's emergency kit!
A containment breach floods the corridor with raw magic, and {name} is hit!
{name} steps on a pressure plate, and an experimental weapon fires!
A mutated specimen breaks free from stasis as {name} passes!
A temporal anomaly snaps shut on {name}, disorienting!
realm.abandoned_laboratory.name: Abandoned Laboratory
realm.shadow_realm.events.ambient.0: Reality flickers. {name} sees double for a moment.
realm.shadow_realm.events.ambient.2: The shadows here seem to breathe. Slowly. Deliberately.
realm.shadow_realm.events.ambient.3: {name} feels something pulling at their mana from below.
realm.shadow_realm.events.ambient.4: A rift in space opens briefly, showing another world. The whole other world stands eerily still.
realm.shadow_realm.events.ambient.5: The ground shifts underfoot. Nothing is solid here. Nothing is trying to be.
realm.shadow_realm.events.discoveries.0: {name} finds crystallized void essence on a dead creature.
realm.shadow_realm.events.discoveries.1: A pocket dimension collapses, dropping its contents.
realm.shadow_realm.events.discoveries.2: {name} absorbs residual energy from a fading rift.
realm.shadow_realm.events.rare.0.text: {name} absorbs a collapsing void crystal, pure essence!
realm.shadow_realm.events.rare.2.text: {name} pulls a glowing lantern from the void. It never goes dark!
realm.shadow_realm.events.rare.3.text: {name} wraps themselves in living shadow, a cloak of concealment!
realm.shadow_realm.events.rare.4.text: {name} snatches a charm from an abyss stalker's fading corpse, carved with the rune of evasion!
realm.shadow_realm.events.traps.0: A void tendril lashes out at {name}!
realm.shadow_realm.events.traps.1: {name} steps through a spatial fold, disorienting impact!
realm.shadow_realm.events.traps.2: Shadow claws rake at {name} from the darkness!
realm.shadow_realm.events.traps.3: A gravity inversion slams {name} into the ceiling!
realm.shadow_realm.name: Abyss Gate
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.0: {name} cannot tell if they are walking on ground or floating.
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.1: The void here is so deep that sound ceases to propagate.
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.2: {name} sees echoes of themselves from other timelines.
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.3: Space folds back on itself. The party passes the same point twice.
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.4: A black sun burns overhead, radiating darkness instead of light.
realm.void_abyss.events.ambient.5: {name} feels their thoughts being pulled apart by the emptiness.
realm.void_abyss.events.discoveries.0: {name} collects crystallized void from a collapsed pocket dimension.
realm.void_abyss.events.discoveries.1: The remains of another expedition float by, their supplies intact.
realm.void_abyss.events.discoveries.2: {name} absorbs energy from a dying rift nexus.
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.0.text: {name} finds an abyss crystal radiating pure primordial essence!
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.1.text: {name} collects runite that has spent aeons in the abyss. It's changed.
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.2.text: {name} wrests a blade from the deep dark. It seems to cut through reality!
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.3.text: {name} pries a gem-encrusted gauntlet from an abyss creature's withered hand. It pulses with stolen life!
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.4.text: {name} discovers an orb containing a trapped dimension, incredible power!
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.5.text: {name} finds a charm pulsing with abyss energy, its power barely contained!
realm.void_abyss.events.rare.6.text: {name} finds a lantern drifting in the deep dark, its flame burning against the void!
realm.void_abyss.events.traps.0: A gravity well inverts, and {name} slams into the ceiling then back down!
realm.void_abyss.events.traps.1: {name} is caught in a temporal loop, experiencing the same pain twice!
realm.void_abyss.events.traps.2: A void creature phases through {name}, draining their life force!
realm.void_abyss.events.traps.3: Reality tears open beneath {name}, who barely avoids falling into nothing!
realm.void_abyss.events.traps.4: An anti-magic pulse hits {name}, disrupting their defenses!
realm.void_abyss.name: Sunken Abyss
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.approachText: The darkness at the center of the chamber condenses. Something that has been here longer than light gazes upon your party.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.defeatText: The Sovereign does not scream. It simply becomes less. The abyss is quieter without it. Somewhat.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.lore: An insect-like entity that seems to be made entirely of shadow. It appears to be the ruler of the abyss, with all denizens of this place treating it with reverence and fear. The most unsettling aspect of the creature is its complete lack of sound, with even its most devastating attacks being completely silent.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.name: The Oblivion Sovereign
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.0.armorT: The Sovereign's void energy absorbs much of the impact!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.0.name: Manifest
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.0.transi: The Sovereign's accumulated mass begins to churn. It is becoming more.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.1.abilit: The Sovereign exhales abyss-dark across the chamber!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.1.armorT: Void energy still cushions the Sovereign's form!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.1.name: Surging
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.1.transi: Something ancient and heavy shifts at its core. It stops holding back.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.2.abilit: The abyss presses inward from all directions!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.2.armorT: Thin tendrils of void still deflect some blows!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.2.name: Unbound
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.2.transi: The Sovereign sheds its shape. What remains beneath is older.
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.3.abilit: Everything the abyss ever swallowed pours out at once!
realm.oblivion_rift.boss.phases.3.name: The Deep
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.0: {name} walks on platforms of solidified nothingness.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.1: The concept of direction has no meaning here, only forward.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.2: {name} sees the end of all things and looks away quickly.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.3: Reality is a thin membrane here. The party can see through it.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.4: Entities vast beyond comprehension move in the distance, unaware of the party.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.ambient.5: {name} feels time flowing backwards, forwards, and sideways simultaneously.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.discoveries.0: {name} gathers essence that has crystallized into impossible geometries.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.discoveries.1: A fragment of a destroyed world drifts by, and {name} salvages from it.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.discoveries.2: {name} absorbs raw oblivion energy from the space between realities.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.rare.0.text: {name} finds a tear in reality leading to a void essence wellspring!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.rare.1.text: {name} plucks a charm from the deep dark. It warps the air around it.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.rare.2.text: {name} tears a cloak of living shadow from the rift wall. It wraps around them instinctively.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.rare.3.text: {name} pulls a helm of abyssal authority from a collapsed vault, its runes still demanding attention!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.rare.4.text: {name} wrenches a plate of abyssal iron from the rift wall, barbed with crystallized shadow!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.traps.0: An oblivion wave washes over {name}, who briefly ceases to exist!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.traps.1: {name} is caught between colliding reality fragments, crushed!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.traps.2: The Sovereign's attention turns briefly to {name}. Even partial focus is agony.
realm.oblivion_rift.events.traps.4: A paradox storm engulfs {name}. Existing and not existing hurts!
realm.oblivion_rift.events.traps.5: {name} is struck by a shard of broken time!
realm.oblivion_rift.name: Oblivion Rift
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.0: The walls here lean inward, as if the space is slowly collapsing toward a point.
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.1: {name} passes a row of altars, each still wet.
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.2: The floor is etched with names in a language no one recognizes.
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.3: Something watches from the dark. It does not approach. It is patient.
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.4: {name} finds footprints leading toward the center. None lead back.
realm.void_hollow.events.ambient.5: The air here has a taste to it. Like metal and old promises.
realm.void_hollow.events.discoveries.0: {name} pries loose a cache of void essence from a cracked altar.
realm.void_hollow.events.discoveries.1: A ledger of transactions lies open on a stone table. The entries are all prices.
realm.void_hollow.events.discoveries.2: {name} finds a vial of something thick and dark. It pulses.
realm.void_hollow.events.rare.0.text: {name} discovers an untapped void essence wellspring!
realm.void_hollow.events.rare.1.text: {name} finds a void contract pinned to a crumbling altar, its terms still binding!
realm.void_hollow.events.rare.2.text: {name} finds a crude effigy stuffed with scraps of void-pact bargains!
realm.void_hollow.events.rare.3.text: {name} discovers a glass eye that has clearly been watching this hollow for a very long time!
realm.void_hollow.events.traps.0: Void energy surges through the floor, scorching {name}!
realm.void_hollow.events.traps.1: {name} brushes against a wall and is briefly drained.
realm.void_hollow.events.traps.2: A dark tendril whips from the shadow and strikes {name}!
realm.void_hollow.name: Void Hollow
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.0: Void entities drift through the chamber, ignoring the party.
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.1: {name} watches two void entities make an exchange. Neither looks pleased.
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.2: Candles float at head height, burning with black flame.
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.3: A queue forms at a door. The things in line do not have faces.
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.4: Every surface here is inscribed with terms and conditions in fine script.
realm.void_sanctum.events.ambient.5: {name} is offered something by a passing figure. They wisely refuse.
realm.void_sanctum.events.discoveries.0: An unclaimed payment sits on a stone counter. {name} takes it.
realm.void_sanctum.events.discoveries.1: {name} finds a chest whose lock is a contract. The terms are reasonable.
realm.void_sanctum.events.discoveries.2: A broker left its ledger unattended. {name} extracts useful materials.
realm.void_sanctum.events.rare.0.text: {name} steals an unclaimed prize from a void broker's table!
realm.void_sanctum.events.rare.1.text: {name} finds a crystallized fragment lodged in the sanctum wall.
realm.void_sanctum.events.rare.2.text: {name} intercepts an undelivered void contract left on a sanctum counter!
realm.void_sanctum.events.rare.3.text: {name} finds a ledger detailing a forgotten trade. The rewards are theirs.
realm.void_sanctum.events.traps.0: {name} triggers a binding ward and is briefly paralyzed!
realm.void_sanctum.events.traps.1: A mana-hungry rune activates under {name}'s feet!
realm.void_sanctum.events.traps.2: An incomplete transaction animates and strikes at {name}!
realm.void_sanctum.name: Void Sanctum
realm.void_heart.boss.approachText: A tall, featureless figure rises from the center of the chamber. It opens a ledger and begins to write.
realm.void_heart.boss.defeatText: The Arbiter closes its ledger. "Agreement terminated." It does not bleed. It simply... concludes.
realm.void_heart.boss.lore: Neither god nor beast. It has mediated the terms of a thousand bargains and held each one to account. It regards your party with the detached interest of an accountant reviewing figures.
realm.void_heart.boss.name: The Void Arbiter
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.0.armorText: The Arbiter's contractual wards deflect much of the damage!
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.0.name: Opening Terms
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.0.transitio: The Arbiter pauses. "An adjustment to the terms. Accept, and the cost of Phase Two is halved. Refuse, and we continue at full price."
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.0.voidPactC: The party accepts the adjusted terms. The Arbiter nods and notes it down.
The party refuses. The Arbiter notes that too.
The Arbiter offers adjusted terms: the whole party takes 20 HP damage, but Phase Two deals half damage. Accept or refuse?
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.1.armorText: Residual wards still absorb some of your attacks!
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.1.name: Amended Contract
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.1.transitio: The Arbiter sets down its quill. "Final offer. One of you accepts significant personal cost. The proceedings end more quickly."
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.1.voidPactC: The terms are accepted. The Arbiter tilts its head, satisfied.
Refused. The Arbiter makes a note in its ledger. The column for "unnecessary expenses" grows.
The Arbiter's final offer: the weakest party member takes 40 HP damage and becomes Void-Drained, but the Arbiter loses 60 HP and is stunned for 2 rounds. Accept or refuse?
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.2.abilities: The Arbiter stamps its seal. Void energy erupts outward!
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.2.armorText: The Arbiter's wards continue to deflect your attacks!
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.2.name: Breach of Contract
realm.void_heart.boss.phases.2.transitio: The Arbiter closes its ledger with finality. There are no more offers.
realm.void_heart.events.ambient.0: The chamber is perfectly silent except for the sound of a quill scratching somewhere.
realm.void_heart.events.ambient.1: The Arbiter's chamber lies ahead. {name} can already feel its attention.
realm.void_heart.events.ambient.2: Old debts hang in the air here like fog.
realm.void_heart.events.ambient.3: {name} reads inscriptions on the walls: terms, conditions, consequences.
realm.void_heart.events.ambient.4: The gravity here pulls slightly sideways. Nothing falls straight.
realm.void_heart.events.discoveries.0: {name} finds a sealed container of void essence, unclaimed for ages.
realm.void_heart.events.discoveries.1: A cache of runite sits behind a door that has no lock. Strange.
realm.void_heart.events.discoveries.2: {name} finds a tribute that was never collected. They collect it.
realm.void_heart.events.rare.0.text: {name} discovers a pre-paid reward awaiting collection!
realm.void_heart.events.rare.1.text: {name} pries a razor-thin sliver of hardened abyss from the chamber wall.
realm.void_heart.events.rare.2.text: {name} finds a signed contract granting extraordinary boons!
realm.void_heart.events.rare.3.text: {name} finds the Arbiter's personal ledger, dropped in haste!
realm.void_heart.events.traps.0: A binding agreement activates, draining {name} of energy!
realm.void_heart.events.traps.1: {name} breaks a deal-seal on the floor, releasing a void burst!
realm.void_heart.events.traps.2: An echo of an old fight replays suddenly, striking {name}!
realm.void_heart.name: Void Heart
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.0: {name} keeps to the treeline as a crusader patrol marches past on the road.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.1: Banners of the High King snap in the wind above a fortified checkpoint.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.2: A temporary encampment sprawls across the valley. {name} can hear orders being barked all throughout.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.3: {name} passes a shrine defaced with anti-magic scripture.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.4: The distant toll of a war-bell rolls across the farmland.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.ambient.5: {name} finds a refugee trail, cold and long abandoned.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.discoveri: {name} raids an unguarded supply wagon left at the roadside.
A tax-collector's strongbox lies forgotten in a ransacked cottage.
{name} finds a deserter's cache hidden beneath a hay bale.
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.rare.0.te: {name} intercepts a crusader pay-chest bound for the front!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.rare.1.te: {name} loots a paymaster's strongbox from a toppled wagon!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.rare.2.te: {name} lifts a merchant's lucky coin from a captured caravan!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.rare.3.te: {name} pries a runic charm from a fallen officer's effects!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.traps.0: A sentry's alarm bell clangs, and {name} scrambles for cover!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.traps.1: {name} stumbles into a field of scattered caltrops!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.traps.2: A crossbow bolt whistles from a hidden murder-hole at {name}!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.events.traps.3: A tripwire snare yanks tight around {name}'s ankle!
realm.kingdom_outskirts.name: Kingdom Outskirts
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.0: {name} slips past a drill yard where recruits rehearse anti-magic formations.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.1: Racks of polished steel line the armory walls, each blade blessed against magic.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.2: A war chapel echoes with a chaplain's recorded sermon, playing to an empty hall.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.3: {name} passes rows of empty bunks, footlockers stamped with the royal crest.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.4: The clang of a distant smithy never seems to stop.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.ambient.5: {name} reads a duty roster pinned to the wall. Half the names are crossed out.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.discoveri: {name} strips a weapons rack of its runic-forged steel.
A quartermaster's ledger reveals a hidden supply cache.
{name} pries open a blessed reliquary and pockets its offerings.
realm.crusader_barracks.events.rare.0.te: {name} cracks open the garrison paychest, a soldier's fortune!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.rare.1.te: {name} clears an armory vault of runic ingots!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.rare.2.te: {name} recovers the drum that once rallied a whole regiment!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.rare.3.te: {name} tears a battle standard from the barracks wall, its enchantments still potent!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.rare.4.te: {name} finds a pair of battle-worn wraps belonging to a legendary berserker, still wrapped around a training post!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.traps.0: A rigged training dummy swings a live blade at {name}!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.traps.1: An oil trough ignites, and flames roar toward {name}!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.traps.2: A portcullis slams down, its spikes grazing {name}'s gear!
realm.crusader_barracks.events.traps.3: A stack of pikes topples from the wall onto {name}!
realm.crusader_barracks.name: Crusader Barracks
realm.palace_fortress.boss.approachText: The throne room doors burst open. The High King rises, blade drawn, eyes burning with conviction!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.defeatText: The High King falls to his knees, his crown clattering across the stone floor!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.lore: The leader of the human kingdoms and commander of the Crusader armies. He is a master swordsman and tactician, using his combat experience to protect his throne himself. He liberally uses his arsenal of legendary weaponry, as well as the lives of his soldiers, to keep his enemies at bay. When pushed to the brink he may even break his own oaths and call upon the power of magic to turn the tide. His defeat will be a major blow to the Crusader forces, leaving our colonists safe to return to their old homes.
realm.palace_fortress.boss.name: The High King
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.0.name: The Duel
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.0.tran: The High King draws a second blade! His fury is unrelenting!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.1.abil: The King cleaves with both blades in a wide arc!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.1.name: Enraged
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.1.tran: The King calls his royal guard to his side!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.2.abil: Royal guards charge into the fray!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.2.name: Royal Guard
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.2.tran: The King shatters his crown! Dark energy surges through him!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.3.abil: The King unleashes a devastating whirlwind of steel!
realm.palace_fortress.boss.phases.3.name: Desperate
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.0: {name} crosses a gilded hall where portraits of dead kings glare down.
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.1: Marble columns rise into shadow, each carved with the history of the Crusade.
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.2: {name} steps around a mosaic depicting the burning of a magic-user.
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.3: Silk banners and golden filigree drip from every archway.
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.4: {name} hears the faint music of a court that fled long ago.
realm.palace_fortress.events.ambient.5: The throne-room doors loom ahead, sealed with the royal sigil.
realm.palace_fortress.events.discoveries: {name} empties a coffer from the royal treasury.
A vault of confiscated magic yields tomes and void essence.
{name} prises jewels from an abandoned ceremonial crown.
realm.palace_fortress.events.rare.0.text: {name} breaks into the royal war chest, a king's ransom in gold!
realm.palace_fortress.events.rare.1.text: {name} raids the vault of confiscated magic, raw void essence!
realm.palace_fortress.events.rare.2.text: {name} claims a lodestone the crown used to draw wealth to its coffers!
realm.palace_fortress.events.rare.3.text: {name} recovers the High King's personal sword from a display case in the war gallery!
realm.palace_fortress.events.rare.4.text: {name} lifts the Commander's Crown from a pedestal in the throne antechamber!
realm.palace_fortress.events.traps.0: A pressure plate springs a wall of gilded spears at {name}!

realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.0: The floor is stone. Then it is not. Then it is stone again.
realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.1: {name} looks left and sees the room they came from. But they came from the right.
realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.2: Something laughs. There is no one there to laugh.
realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.3: The walls are crystal, then shadow, then crystal. It hurts to watch.
realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.4: {name} notes that their footprints lead away from where they are standing.
realm.fracture_gate.events.ambient.5: A door opens onto a wall. A wall opens onto a door.

realm.fracture_gate.events.discoveries.2: {name} finds resources that may or may not be from this realm.
realm.fracture_gate.events.rare.0.text: {name} finds a pocket of stable space with unclaimed loot inside!
realm.fracture_gate.events.rare.1.text: A crack in reality reveals a pristine chaos shard!
realm.fracture_gate.events.rare.2.text: {name} pulls a blade from a fracture in space. It exists in two states simultaneously.
realm.fracture_gate.events.rare.3.text: {name} finds a plate of iron forged at the fracture point, chaos still humming through it!
realm.fracture_gate.events.rare.4.text: {name} seizes a pair of boots from a collapsing pocket dimension, still vibrating with speed!
realm.fracture_gate.events.traps.0: The floor inverts briefly, slamming {name} against the ceiling!
realm.fracture_gate.events.traps.2: {name} walks through a door and exits through a different one, moving fast!
realm.fracture_gate.name: Fracture Gate
Every chamber looks exactly like the last one.
{name} marks a wall. Two turns later it is unmarked. Two turns after that it is somewhere else.
The labyrinth is not trying to trap the party. It simply does not remember what it looked like.
{name} hears their own footsteps coming from the other direction.
A sign on the wall reads "EXIT." It has been wrong twice already.
The ceiling is further away than it was. Or nearer. It is difficult to say.
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.discover: {name} finds a room that wasn't here a moment ago. It has loot in it.
A cache tucked in a corner that the labyrinth has been carrying around.
{name} backtracks and finds something that was not there on the way out.
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.rare.0.t: {name} finds a still point in the chaos, a perfectly calm room with valuable loot.
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.rare.1.t: A seam in the labyrinth wall reveals a chaos shard, perfectly intact despite everything!
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.rare.2.t: {name} spots an unraveler's eye embedded in a wall, watching nothing in particular.
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.traps.0: The floor dissolves briefly under {name}'s feet!
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.traps.1: A wall closes faster than expected, striking {name}!
realm.shifting_labyrinth.events.traps.2: A corridor shortens suddenly, hurling {name} against its end!

realm.unraveling_core.boss.approachText: Something at the center of the core shifts. Parts of it are in different places than other parts. It has too many edges. It turns toward the party, and the turning takes longer than it should.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.defeatText: The Unraveler disperses. Each thread of it unwinds back into the labyrinth it came from. Somewhere, something subtle changes.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.lore: A giant floating eyeball that seems to be a master of illusion. Using the chaotic energies of the labyrinth, it is able to mask itself as other powerful entities that it pulls from the minds of the colonists. It makes chaotic use of our previous foes' abilities, though it thankfully cannot hold these forms for long while being attacked.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.name: The Unraveler
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.0.abil: A chaos pulse detonates outward from the Unraveler!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.0.armo: Chaos energy refracts your attacks, absorbing your damage!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.0.name: Incoherent
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.0.tran: The Unraveler fractures into shards then snaps back together. It looks a little different.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.1.abil: A chaos pulse detonates outward from the Unraveler!
A fragment splits off and takes shape!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.1.armo: The chaos field is thinning but still deflects some blows!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.1.name: Fracturing
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.1.tran: The Unraveler sheds one version of itself. What remains is faster and angrier.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.2.armo: Flickering chaos energy still absorbs a fraction of your damage!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.2.name: Unbound
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.2.tran: The Unraveler stops pretending to have a stable form. Every round from here is different.
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.3.abil: The Unraveler tears reality apart around the party!
An unraveling force seizes the party!
realm.unraveling_core.boss.phases.3.name: The Last Thread
realm.unraveling_core.events.ambient.1: {name} exists. Then more than one of them exists. Then just one again.
realm.unraveling_core.events.ambient.2: The center of the labyrinth is visible in every direction at once.
realm.unraveling_core.events.ambient.4: A thought {name} had yesterday plays out on the wall in front of them.
realm.unraveling_core.events.ambient.5: Everything is fine. Everything has never been fine.
