story_milestone.colony_10.text:
You think back to how this community began. We were small and scared, nearly starving through our first winter. You've all grown much stronger, in body, mind, and spirit. Your efforts to lead this community are paying off in spades.

You still have to keep pushing. The Crusade is looming on the horizon and your community needs to be ready to face them when the time comes.
story_milestone.colony_10.title: A Thriving Community
story_milestone.colony_5.text:
Your community is still small, but growth is steady. You anticipate more will join as you advance your ability to harness magic. Until then, you do what you can for those who've already made this colony their home.

Despite the progress, you still find yourself thinking back to The Crusade each night. One day you hope to bring your new friends back to the homes that were taken from them.
story_milestone.colony_5.title: A Settlement Forms
story_milestone.first_bufos_colonist.tex:
A foreign presence in the world. The bufoi are a group of people that resemble frogs, salamanders, or even occasionally fish, but with a more human-like body plan. They are by far the furthest removed group of people from the other races, with humans having little understanding of how the bufoi live their lives. Some even go as far as assuming the bufoi are not truly intelligent beings, though anyone who's lived among them knows that this is preposterous.

Despite not being inherently magical beings themselves, the bufoi still found their communities targeted by the spreading Crusade. They were flushed from their homes and forced to move downstream, into the far reaches of The Frontier. While the newly formed communities there are willing to take in these bufoi, their strange behaviors are quickly seen in full.

It is unclear if the bufoi are amphibious, like the animals they resemble. Regardless, it is well known that they tend to live near fresh water sources like rivers and lakes. Their society is often viewed as the most foreign part about them, even more so than their physical appearance. For example, their courtship traditions are known to confuse and often frighten humans who find themselves in the wrong place at the wrong time. Despite these differences, the bufoi have had little trouble fitting in among communities in The Frontier. Some may find it odd when they spend their leisure time soaking in nearby rivers or fall asleep at odd hours of the day, but their friendly nature tends to make them seem normal among their community of outcasts. So friendly in fact that rumors have begun to spread of a bufos finding his true love among the ferini people.

It can often be difficult to guess how a bufos is feeling, but overall, much like the ferini, they always seem content living in the far off parts of The Frontier. They almost always enjoy life among their newly found community and seem to take great joy in teaching their interested neighbors about their people.
story_milestone.first_building.text:
Your group has staked their claim in the wild frontier. Few others live in these parts, but you'll keep your doors open for traders and wanderers who stumble past.

With this seclusion you hope to build a thriving community while you wait out the growing crusade in your homelands. Here we will be able to practice magic freely and attempt to reclaim knowledge that's been lost to time.
story_milestone.first_building.title: First Foundation
story_milestone.first_crusader_raid_surv:
You hadn't anticipated crusaders making it this deep into the frontier. Thankfully you were prepared, pushing back the invaders for the time being.

Their presence shakes the whole colony. Rumors spread that greater forces will be sent our way in the near future. We'll need to be prepared for anything.

It may even be time to use our progress to slow down the crusade. Perhaps we could open a rift right into the heart of the kingdom and cut off their supplies from there? The dangers will be colossal, but we'll do what we must to keep our frontier safe.
story_milestone.first_death.text:
Today a colonist has died. This will take a major toll on the friends they've made over their time here. Another may one day take their place in the colony, but this loss will be felt for a very long time.

We'll do what we can to keep the remaining colonists safe. Fight in groups, always wear armor, try out ranged weapons, and keep an abundant supply of healing potions.
story_milestone.first_death.title: The First Marker
story_milestone.first_ferin_colonist.tex:
A people with a strong connection to the wilderness. The ferini have always found themselves on the outskirts of society, living among themselves and the animals they befriend in far off lands. The Frontier is comfortable for the ferini, acting as many communities' home for years already.

The ferini largely live their lives unseen by other groups of people, content to live among their own and let the land provide for them all that they need. Ferini communities tend to differ a lot between one another, with some making their homes in steep mountains among the goats, others with deer in the woods, all sharing a reverence for nature.

This deep understanding of nature has manifested in the ferini through gifts from the world. They find themselves gifted with traits much like the animals they live among and the ability to communicate directly with the wild things around them. The few humans who are aware of the ferini outside of myths treat these gifts as curses, shunning the ferini from human society completely.

As The Crusade spreads, the ferini find their homes encroached upon by fearful humans. To keep themselves safe they've moved deeper into The Frontier, further from the homes they've grown alongside. They hope to one day return to these homes regardless of the damage the Crusaders continue to inflict upon the land. For the time being they find themselves joining new settlements, helping their small communities of strangers work alongside the unfamiliar nature that surrounds them.
story_milestone.first_friend.text:
Some of your colonists have become fast friends. You see these two chatting 
        often, keeping each other sane during these unstable times.
story_milestone.first_friend.title: Friendly Neighbors
story_milestone.first_human_colonist.tex:
A dominating presence in the world. Humanity makes up the largest portion of the known world, living in kingdoms that span huge swaths of land. Known for their strict rules and social boundaries, humans tend to have a skewed perception of the world outside of their borders that fails to conform to their requirements.

With these codes of conduct came an air of superiority over the other. This arrogance has led the kingdoms to outlaw magic completely, along with those who are born with it. Their passion to enforce their rules has culminated in The Crusade, an attempt by humanity to rid their world of magic completely.

Nearly all of the kingdoms throughout the realm have pushed aside their grudges to work together on this common goal. It has been rather easy to convince the people under these rulers to contribute to the cause, with many being taught from a young age to be fearful of the other. With the ever expanding Crusade on their heels, most magical races have gone into hiding deep within The Frontier, which no kingdom has claimed as its own.

While all Crusaders are human, not all humans are supportive of their actions. Some remember happier times where they had toiled alongside magical beings. Some simply remain unconvinced that further eradication is necessary now that these beings have fled into hiding. Speaking out against The Crusade is forbidden, with those accused of such actions often finding themselves among those they tried to defend in The Frontier. Thankfully these humans are welcomed into their new communities with open arms.

Humans tend to be very different from one another, often being some of the first people to pick up a new skill if they have enough interest in it. With enough effort any human can become a valuable asset to their community. Interestingly humans have no issues learning how to control magic and cast spells despite their lack of innate magical gifts. Truly humans are capable of anything as long as they have the right support from those around them.

We can only hope that these kinder humans are able to prosper.
story_milestone.first_kobalos_colonist.t:
A roguish people known for their bright chromatic skin tones and ears as wide as their own heads. For most humans, the kobaloi are best known for their depictions in myths and stories. For them, a kobalos is a mischievous figure that's as likely to pull a prank on you as they are to eat you whole, especially if you're a child exploring the woods all alone.

In spite of these stories, the kobaloi are a rather peaceful people. Embodying the idea that it takes a village to raise a child, they take any opportunity to help their community. It is clear that they take great pride in their large families and friendly neighbors.

The human kingdoms refused to see this reality and it was only a matter of time before The Crusade made its way to the kobaloi's doors. They defended their communities fiercely, with several groups of kobaloi continuing to fight back against the Crusaders today. While lacking in numbers compared to their attackers, they make great use of their knack for tricks by leading groups of Crusaders into traps and winning battles through ambush tactics.

The many kobaloi who were unable to continue fighting found themselves pushed deep into The Frontier. Their once thriving communities were shattered and each individual was left to pick up the pieces. It wasn't long before many new communities were established, often consisting of complete strangers. These kobaloi continue to be protective of their community, regardless of how different their new neighbors might be.
story_milestone.first_love.text: You overheard some talks of romance among the colonists. It's beautiful to think that they're able to find love so far from home. You can only hope that this relationship helps these two weather the tribulations of The Frontier.
story_milestone.first_love.title: Love on the Frontier
story_milestone.first_mental_break.text:
Today a colonist has lost control of themselves. We all knew that life on the frontier would be difficult, but the constant toil is often too much to bear.

Perhaps we can find ways to keep everyone happy? Better sleeping quarters and consistent access to cooked food are a good starting point.
story_milestone.first_mental_break.title: The Breaking Point
story_milestone.first_nymph_colonist.tex:
A secretive presence throughout recorded history. The nympha are a group of very few, with their hidden communities making them appear even smaller to those unfamiliar with their communities. Living among forest canopies, the nympha are truly one with the magic of the world they live in. Just as the world has become less magical, the nympha have dropped in number, being only a small fraction of what they used to be.

Among modern humans the visage of the nympha brings to mind long standing fears of the unknown, seeing them as symbols of the wicked magic that they've been raised to distrust. One reason often cited for their fears is the nympha's uncanny appearance, with many sightings by humans describing their beauty as otherworldly. Some even fear that nympha may be able to live silently among their communities, acting as a curse upon their friends and family.

In the far past it was not uncommon to see a nymph working alongside humans. While not quite as physically capable as the average human farmhand, the nympha used their magic creatively to bridge the gap. Nympha were sought after by many among humanity's most powerful at that time, making use of the nympha's many talents. It was not uncommon to see nympha employed as bookkeepers, court magicians, or even concubines. Some especially long-lived nympha have fond memories of their time among humans. These nympha still hold out hope for humanity, taking in the exiles that wander into The Frontier.

The many humans that continue to fear the nympha continue to drive them further from their homes in the woods outside of the human kingdoms. The Frontier remains one of the only safe havens for these people, letting them rebuild their communities that were shaken by The Crusade.
story_milestone.first_raid_survived.text:
Not all people are friendly out in the frontier. For every group of traders there is a gang of raiders ready to take what they need by force.

Your small group has held off their attackers today, but you know there will be more in the future. Though no one wants to fight their fellow man, many colonists admit that better weapons and armor would go a long way to make them feel safer.
story_milestone.first_spell.text:
One of your colonists cast their first spell. Whether innate or learned, you 
        are excited by the results. You plan to write more tomes and help everyone 
        get to the point where they can cast their very own spells for the first time.
story_milestone.first_spell.title: The Spark of Magic
story_milestone.first_tame.text:
The Binding Circle was a huge success! Your colony's first animal companion
        has joined the flock and now lives among us. This animal will provide a lot
        to our community as long as we care for it properly.
story_milestone.first_tame.title: Kindred Spirits
story_milestone.first_trade.text:
The trader was one of the first friendly faces your colonists had seen in some
        time. They were excited by all of the trader's goods, but such luxuries would
        remain out of reach for some time.
story_milestone.first_trade.title: Wandering Traders
story_milestone.first_wave_complete.text:
It was horrifying, but opening these rifts may just be a worthwhile endeavour. Your colonists held fast against the horde of fleshy monsters that poured from the portals, finding time to harvest a shadowy material from beyond the rift.

Some of the colonists have turned to calling this material Void Essence which is only fitting for something taken from such unnatural creatures. Your initial tests show that this essence will be of great use to the colony, but it seems that the only way to get it is to re-open the rifts to this terrifying place.

You ponder the dangers, afraid that the only way forward is to once again invite these monsters into your home. Perhaps with enough study the essence will give your colonists what they need to face these beasts with confidence.
story_milestone.first_winter_feast.text:
Winter has arrived and the colony is feeling optimistic. By the first frost we were able to secure plenty of food to last through the season. In their excitement, the colonists proposed a feast to celebrate their hard work.

The Winter Feast is a common tradition throughout the world, though everyone celebrates it differently. What all could agree on was coming together in the warmth of the town hall, fires stoked high.

For one night the harsh winter chill was felt by no one. In lieu of traditional foods, the colonists shared a meal of roasted vegetables, fresh bread, and a hearty stew. The meal was simple and made with care.

The whole feast was over in a matter of hours, but the memories will last a lifetime. This group of strangers will continue to weather the cold together.
story_milestone.first_winter_feast.title: Winter Celebration
story_milestone.realm_abandoned_laborato:
Of the buildings left in the untouchable zones, this laboratory is the most well preserved. It looks almost trapped in time, left exactly as it was before the Crusader occupation. The inside is a lot less orderly, with halls twisting chaotically throughout in a way that doesn't quite add up to the building's exterior.

Many important experiments took place here and their remnants continue to linger. Forms of pure chaos roam throughout the laboratory, protecting the valuable research that must lie deep within the ever-extending building.

The defeat of the experiment calmed the chaos throughout the laboratory. Scouring research notes became possible after this, allowing the long dead researcher's work to continue on in a place where it will be appreciated.
story_milestone.realm_ancient_university:
The main doors of the library open up to the large university grounds it was built upon. This university was once on the cutting edge of magical research, a place sought out by magicians from all over the world.

Now it lies in ruins, the few remaining buildings being converted to encampments for the Crusaders that occupy the grounds. Interestingly, some portions of the university are left untouched by the Crusaders, with the library included. These off-limits areas hold magical secrets that even the Crusaders decided weren't worth dealing with.
story_milestone.realm_arcane_library.tex:
An abandoned library full of arcane knowledge. The only sound heard throughout the library is the sweeping of brooms that seem to be moving on their own, keeping the library tidy despite the lack of visitors.

Other magical creations stalk the halls, keeping roughhousing to a minimum with the remnants of magical energy they still possess. No one can blame them for continuing their work, but it makes hunting for useful tomes quite difficult when all visitors are treated as intruders.
Just before the castle gates lie the training grounds of the Crusader forces, a barracks stocked with weapons and armor. Thankfully only a small reserve of Crusaders remain on guard, with the rest marching on the front lines of their campaign.

The barracks seem to be the only way into the castle itself, with the main gates being far too heavily guarded to pass through. Destroying the barracks not only gives access to the castle, but also to their equipment and supplies, hurting their efforts on the frontier.
story_milestone.realm_crystal_caves.text:
A network of tunnels full of large crystal deposits. A handful of creatures make the chambers of the caves their home, but the majority of the tunnels are empty and relatively safe, assuming you can stomach a tight squeeze.

Strangely, there seem to be no signs of a cave entrance, only allowing for downward exploration. Thankfully, that still leaves a lot to explore.
story_milestone.realm_crystal_depths.tex:
Past the edges of the mines, the tunnels continue downward, spiralling into the depths. The tunnels open into a large expanse of chambers, all covered entirely in crystal formations.

The crystals here glow brightly, making this the brightest part of the whole cave system, and the crystals seem to almost pulse with life. The source of these crystals is found in the heart of these depths, slowly infusing itself into both the rocks and the creatures of the caves.

The defeat of the crystal heart seems to have halted the growth of the crystal formations. The imbued animals seem calmer, their crystal spines breaking apart over time.
story_milestone.realm_crystal_mines.text:
The deeper reaches of the caves spill into a complex system of long abandoned mine tunnels. The mines are much livelier than the caves, with strange crystal-infused beasts making use of the additional space carved out by the miners of the past.

The ground is littered with the remnants of mining equipment and even crystalline golems that have been left behind to continue the miners' work.
story_milestone.realm_fracture_gate.text:
A gate leading to a fractured realm, not unlike the chaotic halls of the laboratory. Each step taken in this realm seems to shift the walls and floors, making navigation nearly impossible.

The creatures that make this place their home seem to make everyone sick to their stomachs. These monsters shift and contort just like the walls, showing no clear true form. Some colonists even swear they recognized a handful of the faces the creatures wore, but their ever-shifting guise makes this hard to confirm.
story_milestone.realm_fungal_hollows.tex:
Large sections of jungle overrun with fungal growths. The trees within seem to rot, leaving a clearing of gigantic mushrooms and a foggy purple haze.

Thankfully the clearing makes re-orienting oneself much easier, with the larger trees in the distance continuing to point toward the heart of the woods. The wandering fungal horrors make these necessary stops in their territory dangerous, with their toxic clouds poisoning any who linger too long.
The outer edges of the human kingdoms, full of cleared forests and farmland. Stone paths lead toward the kingdom's gates, though they remain far off on the horizon.

The only option is to continue forward one step at a time, avoiding the attention of the laboring villagers. Soldiers patrol the roads and forests, making a peaceful journey to the castle gates nearly impossible.
story_milestone.realm_oblivion_rift.text:
Strangely, the abyssal ocean seems to suddenly end here, a massive waterfall plunging into the incomprehensible blackness below. On the edge of the waterfall is a rocky outcrop hosting an unprotected rift gate.

The master of this shadowy realm lies just beyond the portal in a castle of black stone, carved with sophistication not unlike that seen throughout the human kingdoms.

The defeat of the ancient master of the black stone castle seems to have no effect. The abyss is still dark and the bug-like denizens of the scattered islands continue their lives as normal.
story_milestone.realm_palace_fortress.te:
An imposing fortress built within the walls of the castle. The architecture is grand and ornate, acting as a palace for the king himself.

Despite the kingdom's fear of magic, the fortress is filled with magical wards and traps under the guise of miracle working. To go along with these protections are the priests that created them, wandering the halls in marvelous white robes.

The king's personal guard also patrols the halls of the fortress. Much like the gaudiness of the other palace decorations, their armor is delicately etched with depictions of historic battles and religious scenes. No expense was spared for the materials their equipment was made of, all looking pristine despite the many scars on the guards themselves.

The defeat of the king marks a change in the tide of the Crusade. Perhaps it is time for our colonists to finally go home?
story_milestone.realm_primeval_canopy.te:
The deepest part of the jungle, where nearly all light is blocked by the thick canopy above. The sounds of snarling beasts echo constantly through the foliage.

In the center of the jungle lives a tree known as the Heartwood. All of the jungle's life stems from this tree, though they've long outgrown their relatively small progenitor. Over the years the Heartwood has withered, with spores taking root in its branches and using its vast network of roots to spread throughout the jungle.

Though the Heartwood itself is sacred, its fungal corruption must be eradicated before it can overrun the entire jungle.

With the Heartwood's defeat, a new sapling sits in its place. This small tree will one day repair the damage caused by the spores.
story_milestone.realm_shadow_realm.text:
While not a gate in the traditional sense, this chasm allows one to venture into the world's abyssal depths.

Within the chasm live shadowy monsters and plant-like eyes rooted to the stone below, all quietly stalking any who enter their territory. They are essentially harmless as long as distance is kept, but the tight ledges of the chasm leave little room for avoidance.
story_milestone.realm_shadow_realm.title: Abyss Gate
story_milestone.realm_shifting_labyrinth:
The chaotic energy of the realm becomes more pronounced the deeper one goes. The shifting walls quickly become a labyrinth, with any adventurer finding themselves turned around constantly.

The creatures here are much more varied compared to those found at the entrance. In addition to their shifting faces, their size and body composition contort just as frequently. For a moment a monster may appear as a person, an animal, or something completely unintelligible.
story_milestone.realm_unraveling_core.te:
The center of the labyrinth holds some sort of core of pure chaos. Despite being in sight, actually reaching the core is a frustrating endeavor as the world continues to change at a moment's notice.

A gargantuan floating eyeball idles in the center of the chaos. Unlike the other creatures of this realm, the eyeball seems to have much more control over the chaotic energy surging around it, its form staying perfectly consistent. As one approaches it becomes much more obvious that this creature is harvesting energy from the magical core that acts as the center of the chaos. What will happen to this realm once the core unravels completely?

The eye wielded the core's chaotic energy with mastery, disguising itself as foes from our past. With its defeat, the broken core can begin the process of regenerating. We can only hope that the damage the monster caused can be undone.
story_milestone.realm_verdant_depths.tex:
A vast jungle, teeming with life. Compared to the frontier, this land is truly untouched by man, with many of its plants and animals being completely undocumented in even the most complete bestiaries of the arcane university.

The trees seem to grow taller and taller the further in one travels, giving a clear indication of forward progress despite the lack of man-made paths.
story_milestone.realm_void_abyss.text:
Deep within the chasm's tunnels lies a vast underwater ocean, small rocky islands dotting its surface. Frightening shades flitter over the waters, lighting up the sea with their spectral forms.

The isles hold many ramshackle structures and underground homes, all housing bug-like creatures that seem to thrive in their abyssal caves.

Thankfully, small boats and rafts litter the shores of each island, making traversal surprisingly simple.
story_milestone.realm_void_abyss.title: Sunken Abyss
story_milestone.realm_void_heart.text:
Far within the sanctum lives the Heart of the Void, a place with unclear purpose and surrounded by twisted creatures forced to remain here for many lifetimes.

The penitent guards of the heart seem to be the most far gone of all. Only skin and bones, their bodies have changed to be better tools for their creditor. These monsters have no humanity left and no thoughts of returning home, unlike many of the earlier inhabitants of the sanctum.

The defeat of the master of the void appears to be impermanent, its body sinking into the void-stone ground upon its apparent death. You make the best of this time, destroying as many pages of its ledger as possible while leading the lucid prisoners back to the surface world.
story_milestone.realm_void_heart.title: Void Heart
story_milestone.realm_void_hollow.text:
A strange place that appears darker than even the pits of the abyss. Lanterns aren't much help, the shadowy air engulfing their light within a few paces.

Magical lights seem to be the only way to navigate this place, but even they don't allow one to see very far. The only way to make forward progress is to find a nearby wall and walk along it.

The wall eventually closes in like a funnel, the opposite wall making itself known by touch first before any light has a chance to reach it. Where the walls meet lies a doorway to somewhere just as dark as this expanse.
story_milestone.realm_void_hollow.title: Void Hollow
story_milestone.realm_void_sanctum.text:
Crawling through the expanse of the hollow leads to a proper structure, devoid of light just like the rest of the realm. The structure appears to be made of a perfectly smooth black material, like a solid block of the void itself.

Unlike the hollow that seemed devoid of life, this place is teeming with noise. Chattering sounds like bone tapping bone echo through the halls, the remnants of this realm's prisoners.

Those who fail to uphold their dealings with the master of this place seem to end up here, paying off their debts for the rest of time. They guard their prison viciously, holding out hope for better treatment by their warden, though it is clear that this will never come to pass.
story_milestone.realm_void_sanctum.title: Void Sanctum
story_milestone.realm_wild_frontiers.tex:
The untouched wilderness, spanning a wide variety of biomes, much like the lands the settlement was founded upon.

The wild frontiers are home to many creatures, some friendly, others dangerous, as well as the occasional encampment of bandits or magical folk. The non-animal populations seem to have spiked in recent years as the Crusade continues to push more people from their homes.
story_milestone.research_advanced_arcana:
Your community is learning quickly with the help of your tomes. You discover more 
        magical spells and put them to paper for your colonists to grow even further.
story_milestone.research_alchemy.text:
Who would've guessed that your crops would have more uses than just
        cooking? You excitedly write up recipes for potions based on each plant's
        properties.
story_milestone.research_alchemy.title: Alchemy
story_milestone.research_arcane_infusion:
Your colony can now create their first Enchanting Table. You're excited
        about the possibilities this brings, letting you start enchanting your
        existing equipment to further boost your colonists.
You find that your colonists are quickly outgrowing the simple tomes
        they create in the workshop. Perhaps this knowledge will satisfy their desire
        to learn.
story_milestone.research_beast_binding.t:
The ancient Ferini were known for their perfection of beast binding, but those arts are largely lost to you. Using the Binding Circle you are able to salvage a portion of that art and work alongside the wildlife of the frontier.

As you practice this art you wonder what else the Ferini knew that you'll have to rediscover.
story_milestone.research_deep_delving.te:
In spite of the dangers you find yourself sending colonists deeper into
        these hostile realms. The deeper they go the greater the rewards become, but
        how will we keep up with the dangers ahead?
story_milestone.research_golem_craft.tex:
Soon your first golem will be up and running, but what do you want it to
        do? Maybe it can act as a beast of burden, taking on the menial labor your
        colonists have been putting in for all these years. It's really too bad a
        single golem can't do everything.
story_milestone.research_herbalism.text:
You're quickly feeling more in tune with the plants of the Frontier. With
        the right care you think your crops will be able to handle much harsher
        conditions going forward.
story_milestone.research_herbalism.title: Herbalism
These lands are rich in untapped leylines full of magical energies. 
        Tapping into that energy is a top priority. Using your knowledge of runes, you 
        develop engraved crystals that will help spread magical energies throughout 
        your colony.
Your mana reserves have been stretched thin, so it's time to innovate.
        With some runic tinkering you're able to get more juice out of each mana
        crystal. Your colonists will be pleased to know that the energy problem
        is solved for now.
story_milestone.research_mana_weaving.te:
Many of your colonists complain about the weight of their metal armors and the toll they take on their ability to control their mana flow. You've come up with a clever solution by infusing lighter fabric with pure mana, increasing their protective capabilities tenfold.

While not quite as protective as runite plates, these robes get the job done. As a bonus they even help the wearer with their own mana control, boosting their magical abilities.
story_milestone.research_masterwork.text:
Your colonists have become masters at their craft. Your equipment is of pristine 
        quality and even distant traders struggle to offer you anything you couldn't 
        simply make for yourself.
story_milestone.research_planar_rift.tex:
While you find great success opening rifts to your colony, you wonder
        what may lie beyond these portals. You quickly find a way to maintain a rift
        to other realms for your colonists to explore, though it'll take a toll on your
        mana reserves.
story_milestone.research_runecraft.text:
Runes are the main way to channel magical energies into equipment. Though a metal sword may be stronger than a stone, a stone with the right rune engraved into it might just turn the tide.

You're certain that runes will be used in all sorts of equipment and workstations going forward, so giving your colonists a good understanding of the fundamentals is a must.
story_milestone.research_runecraft.title: Runecraft
story_milestone.research_trade_routes.te:
You've learned from your encounters with traders in the past. You know 
        what they like, what they don't, and how to push them towards better deals. 
        Beyond that your community has become better known and has been included 
        as an important stop on the major trade routes in the frontier.
story_milestone.research_void_architectu:
Your colony has found even more uses for the void essence you collect. By
        hardening our walls and doors with the stuff we'll be able to hold off large
        groups of enemies with ease.
story_milestone.research_void_forging.te:
Harnessing void essence to its full potential, you can now create equipment 
        to rival the weaponry of the far off crusaders. It'll be difficult to find 
        enough of this material to supply your entire colony, but it's not impossible.
story_milestone.research_void_sorcery.te:
While some focus on the brute strength of swords and clubs, you find yourself pondering more delicate options. By manipulating void essence in just the right way, you can use it to enhance a colonist's magical abilities.

Whether using a wand, stave, or dagger, you know these powerful casters will accomplish great things for their colony going forward.
Progress in your colony has rapidly slowed. Perhaps it's time to seek 
        something new to continue your growth. Using your knowledge of rifts, you think 
        you may have found a way to tap into the void itself without ever having to 
        leave your realm. The solution: summon it directly to you.
story_milestone.research_warding.text:
Your first ward: The Arcane Sentinel.

For only a small amount of mana you can properly protect your colony from attacks. You feel that this will come in handy if your colony ever decides to open their gates to dangerous enemies.
story_milestone.research_warding.title: Warding
story_milestone.void_nexus_built.text:
The Nexus is a magical device built to connect your colony to the Void. As soon as it was supplied with mana 
        it began to hum with energy, emitting a small amount of black fog that rolls from the Nexus to the ground. 
        The fog seems to be harmless, but the thinning of the veil between your realm and the Void is clearly noticeable 
        throughout the colony. You feel a need to exercise caution when using this device as the consequences of opening 
        a line of communication, let alone a doorway, to the Void are unknown.
story_milestone.void_nexus_built.title: The Nexus Stirs
The entity from the Void seems to now see your colony as a reliable business partner. Communication channels are open and the entity 
        has no issues reaching out whenever it needs something from us, offering fair payment in return. You feel a lot more confident in 
        your dealings, but it still occasionally asks for something far too outlandish to accept. You must continue to be cautious of this thing.
story_milestone.void_whisper_first_accep:
Something powerful from the Void has taken notice of your colony and the thin veil between your realms. It seems to be an entity of extreme lawfulness, offering pacts and bargains to your colony for completing very specific requests.

Thankfully it does not appear to be able to cross over into our realm, but its pacts are not without consequence. What it asks for is what it will get, threatening extreme punishment if your colony fails to deliver. You must be careful in your dealings with this entity, though some of its deals may be too good to pass up.
story_milestone.void_whisper_refused_3.t:
The entity from the Void seems displeased with your colony's refusal to work with it. It seems understanding of your hesitation, 
        but it is clear that it will not be so forgiving if you continue to refuse its requests. You must be careful in your dealings 
        to keep this entity occupied.
story_milestone.void_whisper_veil_parted:
The entity from the Void has offered to show the colony a glimpse of what we've been working with all this time. Upon receiving payment, it seemed to beam images directly into the minds of your colonists. Everyone was shocked by the sights, with many describing the Void and this entity as horrific, something that may have been better left unseen.

It's clear that this entity holds your colony in high regard, but making deals with something so alien and unknowable is difficult to justify. As your colonists recover from the invasion of their minds, you must decide if working with this entity is worth the risk of further exposure.
story_milestone.waves_10_complete.text:
Your colony has become proficient in battling the monstrous creatures from the Void, holding back all of their attacks whenever the 
        realms were connected. Perhaps your colonists are ready to venture into the Void themselves instead of always letting it come to them. 
        You only hope that the entity from the Void will not keep too close of an eye on your colony as you venture into its realm.
story_milestone.waves_10_complete.title: The Entity Watches

tutorial.attunement.description: Spells only autocast from the one school a colonist is attuned to. Open Priority [P], switch to the Attunement tab, and click a school in each colonist's row. Give colonists different schools so your colony can cast a wider range of spells: a healer, a battle mage, a summoner. A ★ marks the attuned school, and you can switch it for free at any time.
tutorial.attunement.description_none: A colonist can learn spells from tomes, but a spell only casts on its own if its school is one they're attuned to. This applies at home and on expeditions. Each colonist attunes to one school at a time. Open Priority [P], switch to the Attunement tab, and click a school in each colonist's row to attune them. A ★ marks the attuned school. Give colonists different schools so that between them your colony can cast a wider range of spells, and pick ones that match the tomes you plan to use. You can switch it for free at any time.
tutorial.attunement.title: Set Magic Attunements
tutorial.bedroom.description: Build an enclosed room (walls on all sides + a door) with a Bed inside. Valid bedrooms give colonists an ongoing mood bonus when they sleep. The same system can be used to make specialty buildings for each of your different workstations.
tutorial.bedroom.title: Build a Bedroom
tutorial.bedroom_bed.description: Last, put a Bed inside the room. You'll find it on the Furniture tab. Once the room is fully enclosed with a door and a bed, it counts as a bedroom, and colonists who sleep there get a mood bonus.
tutorial.bedroom_bed.title: Place a Bed
tutorial.bedroom_door.description: A room needs a door so colonists can walk in. Pick Door from the Walls & Floors tab and place it in the gap in your wall.
tutorial.bedroom_door.title: Add a Door
tutorial.bedroom_walls.description: Colonists sleep better in a proper room. Build wooden walls around a small area and leave one gap for a door. Click and drag to place a line of walls. The yellow box shows a suggested spot.
tutorial.bedroom_walls.title: Build Bedroom Walls
tutorial.colony_growth.description: Your colony has room for 3 colonists. The cap rises as you reach milestones: surviving Void Nexus waves, venturing into new realms and conquering realm chains. The Rifts panel shows the next one. The Glossary (Settings, View Glossary, under Colonists & Needs) has the full list of milestones that raise the cap. With room to spare, wanderers who come by can join you.
tutorial.colony_growth.title: Growing the Colony
tutorial.cook.description: Press [C] or click Craft in the mode bar, then queue "Cook Meal". Meals restore more hunger and give a mood bonus. Tip: set an auto-cook target at the bottom of Craft's Food & Potions tab so colonists cook more meals on their own when stocks run low.
tutorial.cook.title: Cook a Meal
tutorial.cooking_pot.description: You started with some wheat and your farm will add more, so it's time to turn it into cooked meals. A Cooking Pot lets colonists cook food that fills them up for longer and makes them happier. Order one to be built from the Build menu's Production tab.
tutorial.cooking_pot.title: Build a Cooking Pot
tutorial.craft_planks.description: Press [C] or click Craft in the mode bar, then queue a "Planks" order. Colonists will turn 2 wood into 3 planks at the workbench.
tutorial.craft_planks.description_none: Planks are a refined material that many buildings need. Press [C] or click Craft in the mode bar, and queue a "Planks" order. A colonist will carry wood to the workbench and make them.
tutorial.craft_planks.title: Craft Planks
tutorial.draft.description: Scouts are approaching the colony. Select a colonist and press Draft All, or press [Q] to draft just the selected colonist. Drafted colonists hold their position and fight anything in range.
tutorial.draft.title: Raiders Attack!
tutorial.equip.description: Click a colonist to select them, then click an empty weapon slot in their info panel to equip one of your crafted weapons. Do this for each colonist. Equipped tools also boost work speed.
tutorial.equip.description_none: Crafted weapons wait in storage until a colonist equips one. Click a colonist to select them, then click their empty weapon slot in the info panel and choose a weapon. Do this for each colonist.
tutorial.equip.title: Equip Everyone
tutorial.equip_tome.description: Click a colonist to select them, then click an empty tome slot in their info panel to equip your crafted tome. The colonist will automatically study the tome as part of their regular research tasks.
tutorial.equip_tome.title: Equip a Tome
tutorial.expedition.description: Open Rifts [V], pick The Wild Frontiers, and add all of your armed colonists to the party before you launch. The panel rates a lone colonist as Dangerous. The party fights on its own and stops now and then for you to make a choice. Keep the difficulty low for your first run. If the whole party falls, you can send everyone out again. Coming home safely from a new realm is a colony milestone and raises your colony population cap, like surviving Void Nexus waves and conquering realm chains. The Glossary (Settings, View Glossary, under Colonists & Needs) has the full list of milestones that raise the cap.
tutorial.expedition.title: Complete Your First Expedition
tutorial.farm.description: Your starting food won't last long. Press [F] or click Farm in the mode bar, then drag on grass to plant wheat or berries. Colonists handle planting and harvesting automatically.
tutorial.farm.description_none: Colonists get hungry, and hungry colonists don't last long, so food comes first. Press [F] or click Farm in the mode bar, then drag across open grass to mark a field. Colonists plant and harvest crops on their own.
tutorial.farm.title: Plant a Farm
tutorial.fight.description: Press [Space] or click the 1x button to unpause and let your drafted colonists deal with them. You can right-click the map to move drafted colonists somewhere better.
tutorial.fight.title: Defend the Colony
tutorial.finish.description: Your colony is up and running. Keep an eye on food, mood and defenses, and stock up before the seasons change. Story [J] tracks your goals. Beyond the Wild Frontiers, other realms open through ancient crypts: find one on the map, break in (right-click a wall in Build mode), and attune the rift anchor inside. Rifts [V] lists what you can reach.
tutorial.finish.title: You're On Your Own
tutorial.gather.description: Designate trees or rocks for your colonists to harvest. Press [G] or click Gather in the mode bar, then drag over trees or rocks.
tutorial.gather.description_none: Everything you build needs materials. Press [G] or click Gather in the mode bar, then drag over trees for wood or rocks for stone. Colonists will walk over and harvest them.
tutorial.gather.title: Gather Resources
tutorial.gathering_circle.description: Expedition parties gather at a Gathering Circle, then teleport into an expedition together, and come back to it when they return. Order one from the Build menu's Arcane tab. Every expedition needs one, scouting included.
tutorial.gathering_circle.title: Build a Gathering Circle
tutorial.not_enough_materials: You don't have enough materials yet. This needs {need}.
tutorial.pan_camera.description: Move the camera with [WASD], the arrow keys, or by dragging with the middle mouse button. The mouse wheel zooms in and out. Touch screens can swipe to move the camera and pinch to zoom.
tutorial.pan_camera.description_touch: Drag the map with one finger to look around, and pinch to zoom in and out. While you are building or farming, one finger draws on the map, so use two fingers to move it.
tutorial.pan_camera.title: Look Around
tutorial.research.description: Open Research [R] and pick a technology to study. {techs} have no prerequisites, so pick whichever sounds useful!
tutorial.research.description_none: Research unlocks new buildings, recipes and abilities. Open Research [R] and press Select on a technology. {techs} have no prerequisites, so pick whichever sounds useful. Colonists earn the points at the Research Desk.
tutorial.research.stuck_help: Research takes a while. To speed it up, build a second Research Desk, or open Priority [P] and set one colonist's Research to 1. You can also skip this step.
tutorial.research.title: Start Researching
tutorial.research_desk.description: A Research Desk generates research points to unlock new technologies. Order one to be built from the Build menu's Production tab.
tutorial.research_desk.title: Build a Research Desk
tutorial.select_colonist.description: Click a colonist, either in the list at the bottom or on the map. Their needs, mood, and gear show up in the info panel.
tutorial.select_colonist.title: Meet a Colonist
tutorial.start_time.description: The game starts paused so you can get your bearings. Press [Space] or click the 1x button to resume the game. You can pause again whenever you need a moment. Remember that orders can be given while the game is paused.
tutorial.start_time.title: Start the Clock
tutorial.stuck_help: This can take a while, since colonists need time to do the work. If nothing is happening, check Priority [P] to make sure the right jobs are turned on. You can also skip this step.
tutorial.threats.description: Raiders and wild creatures will come for the colony eventually. Blight can spread through your crops. The game pauses on its own when a raid starts, and you can change that in Settings. Colonists fight with whatever they have equipped, so next you'll arm everyone. A few scouts will test your defenses once you're ready.
tutorial.threats.title: Prepare for Trouble
tutorial.tip.first_winter: Winter is two days away. Crops stop growing in winter, so stock up now: plant extra fields while you still can, build Food Chests (Furniture tab) to slow spoilage, set an auto-cook target in Craft's Food & Potions tab, and put a campfire where colonists spend their time so they don't freeze outside.
tutorial.tome.description: Open Craft [C], find the Tomes section, and craft any spell tome. Your colonists can learn a wide variety of spells that can help grow your colony.
tutorial.tome.title: Craft a Tome
tutorial.undraft.description: Drafted colonists stand at the ready and won't do any work. Select a colonist and press Undraft All so everyone goes back to their jobs.
tutorial.undraft.title: Stand Down
tutorial.v_bedroom.title: Build a valid bedroom
tutorial.v_expedition.title: Send out an expedition (Rifts [V])
tutorial.v_gathering_circle.title: Build a Gathering Circle (Arcane tab)
tutorial.v_research.title: Start a research project
tutorial.v_tome.title: Equip a spell tome
tutorial.v_weapon.title: Arm a colonist
tutorial.weapon.description: Open Craft [C], find the Weapons section, and craft a weapon for each colonist. The x5 button queues several at once. A Stone Spear only costs 2 stone and 1 wood.
tutorial.weapon.description_none: Your colonists will need to defend themselves from raiders, and unarmed colonists fight with their fists. Open Craft [C], find the Weapons section, and craft a weapon for each colonist. The x5 button queues several at once, and a Stone Spear only costs 2 stone and 1 wood.
tutorial.weapon.help_club: Short on stone? A Wooden Club needs only {cost}.
tutorial.weapon.title: Craft Weapons for Everyone
tutorial.welcome.description: You lead a small group of colonists. They handle the work on their own. You decide what gets farmed, gathered and built, and they get to it. Nothing happens instantly, so give them a little time.
tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome to Rifthold
tutorial.work_priorities.description: Every colonist starts with a specialty, shown by the 1s in the grid. Open Priority [P] and click any cell to change how much a colonist cares about that job. 1 is the highest priority, 5 is the lowest, and a dash turns the job off.
tutorial.work_priorities.description_non: Colonists pick their own jobs, and the Priority panel [P] decides what they reach for first. Every colonist starts with a specialty, shown by the 1s in the grid. Click any cell to change it. 1 is the highest priority, 5 is the lowest, and a dash turns the job off for that colonist. If a job isn't getting done, raise its priority.
tutorial.work_priorities.title: Set Work Priorities
tutorial.workbench.description: A Workbench lets you craft planks, tools, and weapons. Press [B] or click Build in the mode bar, select "Production", and place a Workbench.
tutorial.workbench.description_none: A Workbench is where colonists craft planks, tools and weapons. Press [B] or click Build in the mode bar, open the Production tab, pick Workbench, and click an empty spot. If you're short on materials, gather some first.
tutorial.workbench.title: Build a Workbench
